flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Commanding a SCLK Change
flight_rule.description: Do not send the TIME_SCLK_SET command.
flight_rule.rationale: This command is intended for use in testing, generally to jump the time to a flight-like value at the beginning of a test. It is not intended to change time in flight.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Sending this command will have the following impacts: It will cause all active sequences to be deactivated. If the change is larger than the time remaining on the command loss timer, then the monitor for that will trip and the spacecraft will enter safe mode. It will cause the active ephemeris (which changes as a function of ground time) to be invalid, meaning that the spacecraft will enter safe mode. If the SCLK change is backward, then it will also increase the wait time for the max time open limit for continuous data products with time open limits specified.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Perform NAND Radiation maintenance on each ECE at least every 6 weeks during Tour
flight_rule.description:
Perform NAND Radiation Maintenance using the following commands on each ECE at least every 6 weeks during tour, unless that ECE string is marked DEAD.
DDM_RADIATION_MAINTENANCE_EFS DDM_RADIATION_MAINTENANCE_BDS
flight_rule.rationale:
To fix correctable errors in the NAND that otherwise may accumulate over time, in particular from SEFIs which the NAND parts are susceptible to. Performing this activity once every 6 weeks should reduce data corruption. The SEEA used 6 weeks as the assumption for data loss analysis.
In addition, this will allow for prevention of charge build-up from permanently damaging NAND parts due to total ionizing dose (TID). However, this is not a driving rationale behind the 6 week threshold, as the nominal expected dose inside the vault is 21krad over the mission, well below the level of concern at 50krad (RDF=1). So the 6 week threshold is considered very conservative from a NAND parts damage perspective.
Performing maintenance regularly will also provide statistics and data on the number of bit flips, which might be useful for future missions.
The TID expected during cruise due to the solar proton environment is estimated to be ~700 rad, RDF=2, and therefore this maintenance is not needed during cruise. Data loss is driven by the Europa environment and is also not a concern for cruise.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Errors in NAND may build up over time, including SEFIs, which can result in science data loss, corruption in the engineering file system, and permanently reduced storage capacity.

reference_info.reference_document: IOM-5131-20-168 Data Loss Analysis

enforcement_method.enforcement_description:
David Tong, 3/29/23:
I think SEQGen is able to implement this flight rule. However, I do need to confirm that SEQGen is able to determine if the ECE string is "DEAD".
Otherwise, based on the AVS-A-0002's description, here is my interpretation.
During Tour, if 'DDM_RADIATION_MAINTENANCE_EFS' is not being executed more that 6 weeks (42 days), SEQGen should issue an error.
During Tour, if 'DDM_RADIATION_MAINTENANCE_BDS' is not being executed more that 6 weeks (42 days), SEQGen should issue an error.
If command 'DDM_RADIATION_MAINTENANCE_EFS' is being executed less than 6 weeks (42 days) since its last execution, SEQGen should reset the timer and continue the monitoring.
If command 'DDM_RADIATION_MAINTENANCE_BDS' is being executed less than 6 weeks (42 days) since its last execution, SEQGen should reset the timer and continue the monitoring.
Within this flight rule, these two commands should be independently check.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Don't use default parameters
flight_rule.description:
Don't send the HDW commands to use the default parameters (HDW_NPM_RECS_WRITE_DEFAULTS or HDW_USE_DEFAULTS_IN_ZOMBIE)
Associated flight rule: CMD-A-0002
flight_rule.rationale: Some default parameters (aka GNC) will not be valid for flight, particularly after calibrations.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Invalid parameters for the mission phase could lead to potential mission-ending consequences.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Do not enable flight test mode
flight_rule.description: Do not send hardware command to enable flight test mode.
flight_rule.rationale:
Flight test mode will prevent receiving gyro data from the IMU and sending commands to instruments. This will lead to a reset loop until flight test mode is disabled, or until PPROM power cycles the ECE string (which will disable flight test mode).
The Online string may take over as Prime at anytime, unless brought up in the stay-online configuration or isolation mode.
flight_rule.violation_impact: The loss of gyro data from the IMU will result in a reset loop.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Prevent sending the hardware command to enable flight test mode.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Power off ECE for at least 10s before turning back on.
flight_rule.description: Ensure a least 10s between the completion of the behavior that turns off the backup ECE (AVS_POWER_OFF_OTHER_STRING) and the initiation of the behavior to power it back on (AVS_CONFIGURE_OTHER_STRING)
flight_rule.rationale: Electronics need time for capacitance to fully bleed off and volatile memory to fully clear. Note the AVS_POWER_OFF_OTHER_STRING behavior may take up to 10 minutes to complete
flight_rule.violation_impact: Backup string may not boot successfully -- will not result in permanent damage or loss of mission -- propose cat-A due to waiver approval authority rationale.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Seqgen should look for delta between commands. Use the more conservative 10 minute delta.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Do not change the FDU CRC
flight_rule.description: Do not change the FDU state via CRC38.
flight_rule.rationale:
FSW to fatal because the FSW check of the FDU states will trip. This will happen on ENABLED to DEFEATED because the monitor is checking CRC states at 1Hz and the monitor runs at 8 Hz. It will also happen on the transition from DEFEATED to ENABLED because the FDU will be out of sync with the FSW monitoring.
FDU = Fault Detection Unit
Note: this can be performed while the string is in Isolation mode (off-nominal scenario, requires waiver).
flight_rule.violation_impact: FSW will fatal

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: SEQGEN will check to see if either of HDW_DEFEAT_FDU_SELFTEST or HDW_ENABLE_FDU_SELFTEST is executed.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Do not send HDW_ENABLE_TEST_MODE command after launch
flight_rule.description: Do not send HDW_ENABLE_TEST_MODE command after launch
flight_rule.rationale:
If FSW comes up in Sys_TEST mode, all Fault Protection is disabled, and would be mission-ending. Two conditions are necessary for this to occur in flight (1) Ground test mode is enabled and (2) NVCRC41 is asserted via the HDW_ENABLE_TEST_MODE command. Ground test mode is disabled by virtue of disconnecting the umbilical at launch. However a single fault in flight could enable ground test mode. Therefore it is imperative to prevent the HDW_ENABLE_TEST_MODE command from ever being sent after launch.
FSW will not perform correctly if it comes up in SYS_TEST mode. FSW may continue to stroke the PPROM watchdogs in SYS_TEST, so PPROM will never swap to the redundant string.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Loss of mission.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Do not transition online BDS to FULL_OPERATIONAL mode
flight_rule.description: Do not send the command AVS_CONFIGURE_BDS with the argument FULL_OPERATIONAL on the ONLINE string or AVS_CONFIGURE_BDS_FORCE with the argument FULL_OPERATIONAL on the ONLINE string.
flight_rule.rationale: FULL_OPERATIONAL is only necessary when collecting science data from instruments. Only the prime string can collect science data from instruments. The command/argument/string combination is not being verified.
flight_rule.violation_impact: This particular command/argument combination will not be verified, so it is unknown what would happen. At best nothing, at worst it would interfere with science activities.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Do not transmit AVS_BDS_NAND_POWER command with ON or OFF arguments
flight_rule.description: Do not send the AVS_BDS_NAND_POWER command with arguments ON or OFF in flight, to the PRIME or ONLINE string.
flight_rule.rationale: These are intended for test only, will not be well verified, and can interfere with other nominal activities. The CYCLE argument is the only one that should be used in flight.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Potential science data loss and interference with commanded BDS activities.

ECR-22948

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Do not send AVS_BDS_NAND_POWER while recording high rate science data
flight_rule.description:
Do not send AVS_BDS_NAND_POWER while recording data to the BDS at a rate higher than 1 Mbps.
The only instruments capable of exceeding this data rate are: - EIS-NAC - EIS-WAC - MISE - UVS - REASON - E-THEMIS - MASPEX - SUDA
One possible way to implement this (that would be more restrictive than the flight rule, but may be acceptable) is to not send this command when any of those instruments are powered on.
flight_rule.rationale: This command will be verified to not cause science data loss only for the case where we are recording at rates lower than 1 Mbps.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Loss of science data

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Periodically power cycle NAND on EMEM
flight_rule.description: Send the AVS_EFS_NAND_POWER_CYCLE command to any ECE at least once during every 8 weeks that it has been continuously powered.
flight_rule.rationale:
NAND SEFIs will accumulate if not cleared with a power cycle, and eventually accumulate to where EDAC cannot compensate, resulting in complete loss of file system contents.
Sending this monthly results in an estimated 0.1% probability of occurrence of file system failure. Sending it every 8 weeks would double that to 0.2%.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Loss of engineering data and interruption of planned activities.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Manage EFS to avoid auto-deletion by volume
flight_rule.description:
The on-board EFS data product storage volume shall be managed to less than 85% of capacity to avoid auto-deleting data.
See associated flight rules: AVS-C-0002
flight_rule.rationale:
One week's worth of EFS data accumulation is ~5%, so managing the on-board EFS storage to stay less than 85 percent will guarantee 2 week's worth of data can be added (in the event of a missed DSN pass) without invoking the auto-delete function. There are three times during the Cruise Phase (of the MEGA trajectory) just inside the 2AU boundary when we are planning on using the FBA and expect to overflow the EFS data storage due to low (10bps) downlink rates. The FSW is hard coded with a 95% threshold to start the autodelete activity (and has an associated 75% threshold to end it). This is provided as a capability to help ground/ops manage data product volume along with other capabilities such as manual data product deletion by ground/ops.
The thresholds are based on data volume available on EFS, which will change as function of bad blocks, etc.
At the time of making this rule, there's no predicted use case during launch, arrival, or tour phases. However, if they should develop, this rule would certainly apply.
flight_rule.violation_impact:
Auto-deletion based on pre-set priorities may result in the permanent deletion of data that is required or desired to be transmitted and analyzed. Auto-deletion will continue to operate until EFS Data Product Partition is <75% full. Actively managing it to 85% will reduce lost data.
Ground operators should preempt this FSW auto-delete function, to ensure data loss is limited to acceptable loses.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description:
ODM to provide a predict of when the 85 percent threshold will be exceeded.
SCOS will send commands to delete Data Products, which are deemed acceptable.
SCOS may update Telemetry Selection Rules, to reduce data volume being recorded.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Manage EFS to avoid auto-deletion, by quantity of Data Products
flight_rule.description:
The number of on-board EFS data products shall be managed to less than 85% of the maximum, to avoid auto-deleting data.
See associated flight rules: AVS-C-0001
flight_rule.rationale:
One week's worth of EFS data accumulation is ~5% of total volume, so managing the on-board EFS storage to stay less than 85% will guarantee 2 weeks' worth of data can be added (in the event of a missed DSN pass) without invoking the auto-delete function. There are three times during the Cruise Phase (of the MEGA trajectory) just inside the 2AU boundary when we are planning on using the FBA and expect to overflow the EFS data storage due to low (10bps) downlink rates. When reaching the upper capacity of EFS, in terms of data volume, it's possible to reach the maximum number of Data Products too. The FSW is hard coded with a 95% threshold to start the autodelete activity (and has an associated 75% threshold to end it). This is provided as a capability to help ground/ops manage data product volume along with other capabilities such as manual data product deletion by ground/ops.
At the time of making this rule, there's no predicted use case during launch, arrival, or tour phases. However, if they should develop, this rule would certainly apply.
As of Feb 2022, the maximum number of Data Products on EFS is 14,600.
flight_rule.violation_impact:
Auto-deletion based on pre-set priorities may result in the permanent deletion of data that is required or desired to be transmitted and analyzed. Auto-deletion will continue to operate until EFS Data Product Partition is <75% full. Actively managing it to 85% will reduce lost data.
Ground operators should preempt this FSW auto-delete function, to ensure data loss is limited to acceptable loses.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: SCOS will send commands to delete Data Products, which are deemed acceptable for deletion.
SCOS may update Telemetry Selection Rules, to reduce data volume being recorded.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Limit on Number of Parameters Saved at Once
flight_rule.description: Do not save more than 5000 new-valued parameters to nonvolatile memory at one time.
flight_rule.rationale: Parameters are saved to NVM by FSW as records (which are also used for certain FSW-internal states). The limit is 20,000 record "slots". More than half of the slots are already in use due to all the parameters and FSW-internal records. The save action requires one empty slot per "new-valued" parameter in order to be successful. "New-valued" means the value being saved is different from the value in NVM. These temporary records are not deleted until the entire save operation is complete. The limit of 5000 parameters per update operation is meant to be large enough to cover the needs of GNC parameter saves.
flight_rule.violation_impact: If the parameters cannot all be atomically written to nonvolatile memory, the command will report failure, and the nonvolatile memory updates will be rolled back. If a parameter update is not successfully performed later, the affected parameters will all revert to their previously-saved values during the next FSW reset.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description:
Procedural steps to ensure successful parameter saving:
The number of parameters with values differing between volatile and non-volatile needs to be tracked, per module and in total.
If DDM_SAVE_SYS_PARAM needs to be commanded, make sure the module being saved (or ALL since that is an option) has a total number of "new-valued" parameters no more than 5000.
If DDM_FILE_SET_SYS_PARAM (with save_to_nvm = TRUE) needs to be commanded, make sure the number of "new valued" parameters in the file is no more than 5000.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Periodic MRAM checkout
flight_rule.description: Periodically calculate checksum of all critical MRAM contents and verify no corruption.
flight_rule.rationale: FSW bugs, or very rarely radiation events, can possibly corrupt MRAM. Consider performing this yearly, prior to JOI (with enough lead time to respond and resolve issues), or after unexplained anomalies. Flight Computer, EMEM, and REU (e.g. not BDS)
flight_rule.violation_impact: If all MRAM copies become corrupted, it can prevent any use of that ECE.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Include these activities in the Mission Plan; develop AVS Activity type definitions and scheduling goals to perform them in flight, describe strategy and timing in the appropriate AVS procedure.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Wait time between new ephemeris upload and EMT DP dump
flight_rule.description: If a load ephemeris command has been dispatched, a 200 second wait time must follow its successful completion before the Ephemeris Management Table Data Product can be dumped.
flight_rule.rationale: The Ephemeris Management Table (EMT) has two buffers. At any given time, one is inactive while the other is active, and the status of each buffer (i.e., as active or or inactive) switches every 100 seconds. EMT updates are always performed on the inactive buffer while data product dumps are always performed on the active buffer. Thus it will take at most 100 seconds (+ 100 seconds if the upload EMT command isn't applied until the next buffer switch) for the updates performed on the inactive buffer to reach the active buffer and be available for downlink.
flight_rule.violation_impact: The data product will not contain the new ephemeris data

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Feed into ops procedure.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Cold Reset REU if Auto-Switch to Default PPROM Bank
flight_rule.description:
If the REU auto-switch to Default PPROM Bank due to PPROM errors, then operator should cold reset the REU.
These are the EVRs that the operator would see. REU_MGR_EVR_HIGH_WRN_LM_CSR4_PRIME REU_MGR_EVR_HIGH_WRN_LM_CSR4_BACKUP.
If this occurs on the backup REU, then power off, wait 10 seconds, then do the power on.
If this occurs on the prime REU, swap primeness of REU, then repeat the above.
flight_rule.rationale:
PFR 211519. FPGA counts the PPROM bank errors. After 2 errors in the same PPROM command list, the FPGA will no longer run the command list.
According to Mike Thielman, the only thing that can credibly cause this in flight is an uncorrectable error in the SRAM, and even the probability of that happening in flight is about 0.001% over the life of the mission. It isn't something we will regularly check for or see. If it DOES happen, the steps for recovering will be documented in the AVS Subsystem Contingency Procedures to reference.
flight_rule.violation_impact:
REU will not swap ECEs in certain fault cases.
Telemetry Collection Tables may not be loaded (leading to loss of engineering telemetry)

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Will be covered in the AVS Subsystem Contingency Procedures.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Do not allow BDS unused space to drop below 25% of original capacity
flight_rule.description: Do not allow BDS unused space to drop below 192Gibits (out of a BOL total of 768Gibits), at the end of an unfiltered recording session.
flight_rule.rationale:
This guideline covers a risk remaining after implementation of ECR-22941.
NAND is susceptible to SEFIs. BDS hardware cannot record to NAND locations if there is a SEFI present. A single SEFI will affect 25% of the BDS capacity.
Therefore, if a SEFI occurs during a flyby, then 25% of the BDS capacity will be temporarily unusable (until the BDS NAND is power cycled).
The 192Gibits figure does not change as the usable BDS capacity decreases over the life of the mission.
It is acceptable for a filter to result in exceeding this, as the worst case is the filter will not complete, and can be re-commanded after recovering from the SEFI.
flight_rule.violation_impact: There is a small (< 1%) probability of loss of science data from a single flyby if this guideline is not followed.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: AVS procedural check.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Track / Alarm NAND cycle counts
flight_rule.description:
These 3 channels should never exceed 10: DDM_MAX_WEAR_DIFF_ENG0 DDM_MAX_WEAR_DIFF_ENG1 DDM_MAX_WEAR_DIFF_DP
These channels should not increase by more than 300 per month (alarm should be raised as soon as this value is exceeded for a sliding 30-day window) DDM_MAX_WEAR_ENG0 DDM_MAX_WEAR_ENG1 DDM_MAX_WEAR_DP FSW_BDS_PHY_STACK_*_TOTAL_ERASE (there are 28 total of these)
flight_rule.rationale: NAND cycle counts are a consumable. The parts used on Clipper are rated for 100,000 program/erase cycles. Nominally, we should not get anywhere near that number. However FSW bugs could cause run-away cycling (this occurred on SMAP in flight). FSW can cause these write cycles to happen so rapidly that it is possibly to go through 100,000 cycles very quickly.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Possible permanent failure of NAND storage (/eng0, /eng1, /dp, and BDS)

relevant_telemetry.description: There are 28 of these...someday somebody can enter the other 27...

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Will be addressed via: - AVS downlink monitoring procedures - AVS contingency procedures (to perform reset) - Consumables process - Alarm limits

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Space for BDS Filtering
flight_rule.description: Do not allow the BDS unused space to drop below (2x+c), where x = maximum volume of data to be collected in the next flyby, and c =3000 MiBytes.
flight_rule.rationale:
The software will not allow a filter to run if the size of the data set to be filtered exceeds the available space, even if the filter operation would not result in filling up that available space. Could lead to a loss of science data. If a flyby will record x bytes, then we also need x bytes free for the filter.
Further, depending on how the filter works out, you could have up to 1 extra stripe from expected for each bin.
Hardware/software corner case issues or modeling issues could result in another stripe per bin more than expected
FSW will not mount the BDS if there are fewer than 16 free stripes.
So c = 96+96+16 stripes
So in order to ensure a filter can run, and still have 16 free stripes, c = (96+96+16) stripes = 208 stripes = 12 MiB * 208 = 2,496 MiBytes.
FYI this is 2.5% of total BDS capacity that is unusable.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Failed command to filter BDS data.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Incorporate in AVS procedures

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Restore REU PPROM bank if a swap to default occurs
flight_rule.description: Ops should monitor the REU PPROM bank, and restore it should it ever switch to the default bank.
flight_rule.rationale: As described in PFR 211519, if the REU ends up in the default PPROM bank, new events can be blocked from executing until the condition is cleared. This means the REU may not respond to an undervoltage signal from the PCDA, etc.
flight_rule.violation_impact: New events can be blocked from executing until the condition is cleared, if a subsequent fault occurs while on the default bank (e.g. 3 fault scenario), then could be mission-ending.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Address in AVS contingency procedures and AVS alarms

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Verify tone selection channel evaluation types match
flight_rule.description: Prior to loading a tone selection file, verify that for each rule, the telemetry channel type matches the evaluation value type.
flight_rule.rationale: If the types of the telemetry channel and the evaluation value do not match, the comparison may not make sense, leading to erroneously asserted or unasserted tones.
flight_rule.violation_impact: The comparison may not make sense, leading to erroneous tones.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Feed into ops procedures.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Prime String Restricted Commands
flight_rule.description: If a command is restricted to the prime string, do not send it to the online string.
flight_rule.rationale: There are commands that can only be sent to the prime string. If they are sent to the online string, they will fail and produce a command error. This does not endanger the spacecraft, but does produce an avoidable command error.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Command would fail and produce a command error

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Parameter transaction sequence command spacing
flight_rule.description: Do not space commands within individual parameter transaction sequences to be 15 minutes or more apart.
flight_rule.rationale: Parameter transaction sequences expire after 15 minutes (get aborted by FSW) if there are no parameter transaction commands for 15 minutes.
flight_rule.violation_impact: If 15 minutes elapses during a parameter transaction sequence with no parameter commands, the transaction will abort and none of the parameters from that transaction sequence will have changed.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: David Tong to determine.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Number of Telemetry Selection Rules
flight_rule.description: The maximum number of Telemetry Selection rules is 8,000.
flight_rule.rationale: This is a limitation is driven by the avionics and flight software system, as detailed in the DDM FDD.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Attempting to load a TSR file that exceed 8000 rules will fail, and attempting to add TSRs to an existing set that result in more 8000 rules will fail.

reference_info.reference_document: DDM FDD D-56148

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Procedural check

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Evaluation Rate of Telemetry Selection Rules
flight_rule.description: No more than 100 rules can be evaluated in each 8 Hz interval. This means if all rules were configured to be evaluated at 8 Hz, there could only be 100 rules total.
flight_rule.rationale: This is a limitation is driven by the avionics and flight software system, as detailed in the DDM FDD.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Avionics will attempt to continue to execute all Telemetry Selection Rules, but some of the rules will end up executing slower than the configuration requests. In the worst case, the slowest Telemetry Selection Rules may not run at all. If this overload occurs, avionics will generate event reports indicating that some rules have not been run in their execution window and when it evaluates a rule late it will generate an event report indicating which rules are running late.

reference_info.reference_document: DDM FDD

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Procedural steps to ensure FR is met; EHA channel for # of 8Hz TSRs to monitor (DDM-0268); rules to test any changes to TSRs in WSTS/STB

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Timing of WAC cover release
flight_rule.description: The WAC cover deployment shall occur no closer to the Sun than 3 AU.
flight_rule.rationale: The WAC is sensitive to direct solar illumination and heating. Analysis demonstrates that solar pointing will not cause damage to the instrument with the cover open at distances >=3 AU.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Sun may cause instrument damage.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: SEQGen will flag an error if "EIS_WAC_DEPLOY_COVER" is executed while the S/C to sun distance is < 3AU.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: GNC Idle Mode during NAC Cover Deployment
flight_rule.description: During NAC cover deployment, GNC shall be in Control Idle Mode.
flight_rule.rationale:
Disturbances from the spacecraft may prevent cover deployment from being completed nominally. EIS Deployments should be performed without disturbances imparted from thruster firings or reaction wheel torques.
Associated flight rule for cover deployment: GNC-C-0029
flight_rule.violation_impact: Cover deployment may not be successful (cover did not fully open and latch, and require contingency retry)

enforcement_method.enforcement_description:
one-time event
- SEQGen will flag an error if "EIS_NAC_DEPLOY_COVER" is executed and the GNC Mode is not in one of these control mode. "GNC_ACS_CTLIDLE_3R" "GNC_ACS_CTLIDLE_3RS" "GNC_ACS_CTLIDLE_ACQ_3J" "GNC_ACS_CTLIDLE_3J" "GNC_ACS_CTLIDLE_CEL"

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Solar array movement during NAC imaging
flight_rule.description: The solar arrays shall be in a fixed orientation during NAC imaging.
flight_rule.rationale:
Jitter caused by movement of the solar arrays will degrade NAC science data.
Associated flight rules related to settling time: GNC-B-0049, GNC-B-0050, GNC-B-0031
flight_rule.violation_impact: Degraded science data

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: NAC Sun in FOV Avoidance when NAC is ON
flight_rule.description: The sun shall not enter the NAC field of view when the NAC is ON
flight_rule.rationale: Analysis indicates that with the Sun in the NAC FOV at solar distances greater than 3 AU, the power of solar illumination impinging upon the NAC detector and individual NAC pixels and the corresponding photocurrent will affect the detector bias, requiring the NAC to be reset (power cycled).
flight_rule.violation_impact: Sun may affect the NAC detector bias requiring the instrument to be reset (power cycled) before science imaging can resume.

reference_info.reference_document:
MOS FDD D-101647
NAC Field of View defined on the NAC MICD (drawing 10414233)

enforcement_method.enforcement_description:
If it is determined that this FR should be implemented in Merlin, here is a potential FOL that can be used to implement it. This FOL description references states, and enforcement will be at the activity planning level in Merlin.
FOL Descriptions: (eis_nac_active = TRUE) AND (sun_fov = TRUE) AND (stray_light_koz = TRUE)
FOL Evaluation Description: List of Windows that contain the times the Sun is within KOZ and FOV. Any Windows that are returned are in VIOLATION.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: WAC Sun in FOV Avoidance when WAC is ON
flight_rule.description: The sun shall not enter the WAC field of view when the WAC is ON
flight_rule.rationale: Analysis indicates that with the Sun in the WAC FOV at solar distances greater than 3 AU, the power of solar illumination impinging upon the WAC detector and individual WAC pixels and the corresponding photocurrent, as well as the instrument thermal load, are safe when the WAC is operating. To preserve observation quality, the instrument or spacecraft should not be oriented such that the sun is within the WAC FOV during imaging.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Sun may degrade observation quality

reference_info.reference_document: WAC FOV is defined on the WAC MICD (drawing 10414234)

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Procedural check

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: NAC Sun in FOV Avoidance when instrument is OFF
flight_rule.description: The sun shall not enter the NAC field of view when the NAC is OFF
flight_rule.rationale: Analysis indicates that with the Sun in the NAC FOV at solar distances greater than 3 AU, the power of solar illumination impinging upon the NAC detector and individual NAC pixels and the corresponding photocurrent, as well as the instrument thermal load, will not cause damage to the NAC when the instrument is off. Notification is needed for awareness in case of science impact to subsequent observations.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Sun may degrade observation quality.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: WAC Sun in FOV Avoidance when instrument is OFF
flight_rule.description: The sun shall not enter the WAC field of view when the WAC is OFF
flight_rule.rationale: Analysis indicates that with the Sun in the WAC FOV at solar distances greater than 3 AU, the power of solar illumination impinging upon the WAC detector and individual WAC pixels and the corresponding photocurrent, as well as the instrument thermal load, will not cause damage to the WAC when the instrument is off. Notification is needed for awareness in case of science impact to subsequent observations.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Sun may degrade observation quality.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: EIS ASRT-150 AIDs mapping to Bin ID
flight_rule.description: Per IICD ASRT-150, Instrument science data packets associated with a Accountability Identifier (AID) should all be assigned the same bin-id in BDS (i.e., all of the data associated with an AID is in a single bin).
flight_rule.rationale:
This approach allows more rapid downlink and assessment of the completeness of an accountable data product since all of the instrument science data packets associated with the AID are in a single BDS bin.
The instrument FSW/FW does not enforce a mapping between packets with the same AID to have the same bin ID. So for the instrument to comply with ASRT-150, they need to enforce this FR in ops instead.
flight_rule.violation_impact:
Multiple BDS bins will need to be downloaded in order to assess the completeness of the AID. Since BDS bins are related to downlink priority, you may need to wait for ALL data in multiple bins to be downloaded to get the complete AID (if they split packets across more than one bin) and assess the completeness of the Accountable Data Product.
Note that whether ASRT-150 is met or not, the science data would still be downloaded and available. However, not complying with ASRT-150 may result in the process of determining whether or not all of the data that was expected as part of an AID more difficult and time consuming.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: The instrument team is the one that should enforce this guideline by checking their command files and products for this implementation before submitting for approval.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: E-THEMIS Radiator Sun Avoidance, ON <3AU
flight_rule.description: When E-THEMIS is ON, the Sun should not be allowed within the E-THEMIS radiator keep out zone (a cone +/- 22.5 degrees around the radiator normal angle of 16.65 degrees from +y towards -z, see the E-THEMIS MICD) for a duration longer than 78 minutes at distances less than 3 AU.
flight_rule.rationale: Excessive solar heating while operating will damage the E-THEMIS focal plane module.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Damage to focal plane module.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: E-THEMIS Telescope Sun Straylight Avoidance <2AU (Cal Flag Closed)
flight_rule.description:
The Sun shall not be allowed to pass through the E-THEMIS telescope field of view (6 degrees of +Y) at a rate slower than 0.3 mrad/sec when the E-THEMIS calibration flag is closed at distances < 2AU.
See associated flight rule: ETHM-A-0004
flight_rule.rationale: Excessive solar heating through the telescope will damage the E-THEMIS Calibration Flag Motor.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Damage to the Calibration Flag Motor, potential blinding E-THEMIS (if made non-operational).

reference_info.reference_document: E-THEMIS PFT violation with Sun in FOV in launch scenario

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: E-THEMIS Telescope Sun Straylight Avoidance <3.1AU (Cal Flag Open)
flight_rule.description: The Sun should not be allowed within a +/- 7 degree cone around +Y when the E-THEMIS calibration flag is open and at distances < 3.1AU.
flight_rule.rationale: Excessive solar heating through the telescope will damage the E-THEMIS filters. Damage occurs if OFF or if ON.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Damage to the filters.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Close E-THEMIS calibration flag before instrument is turned off
flight_rule.description:
Use only the ETHM_POWER_OFF command to power off E-THEMIS in order to close the E-THEMIS calibration flag prior to powering off the E-THEMIS to provide solar intrusion protection when < 3.1 AU. Do not use the ETHM_POWER_OFF_IMM command to power E-THEMIS off.
See associated flight rule: ETHM-A-0002 and ETHM-A-0003
flight_rule.rationale: The E-THEMIS detector can over heat and potentially be damaged if sun shines down the boresight when the calibration flag is open.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Damage to the detector.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: E-THEMIS power on before science observations
flight_rule.description:
E-THEMIS should be powered at least 4 hour prior to the start of E-THEMIS science observations.
See associated flight rule ETHM-B-0008.
flight_rule.rationale: The Instrument focal plane detector needs to be at its operating temperature and thermally stable in order to return calibrated images.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Degraded science observations

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Include in the constraints used in Merlin for defining the flyby sequence

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: E-THEMIS Telescope Sun Straylight Avoidance Science Observations
flight_rule.description: The Sun shall not be allowed to pass through the E-THEMIS telescope field of view (7 degrees of +Y) when the E-THEMIS calibration flag is open and E-THEMIS is ON during Science Observations.
flight_rule.rationale: Stray solar light in the instrument field of view will degrade the science observations.
flight_rule.violation_impact: some degradation to science data -- not a restriction, just want notification of this condition to correlate.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Feed into ops procedure.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Close E-THEMIS calibration flag before instrument is turned off
flight_rule.description:
The E-THEMIS calibration flag should be closed by using the ETHM_POWER_OFF command to power off the E-THEMIS to provide solar intrusion protection when >3.1 AU. Do not use the ETHM_POWER_OFF_IMM command to power E-THEMIS off.
See associated flight rule: ETHM-A-0004
flight_rule.rationale: The E-THEMIS detector will heat up if the sun shines down the boresight when the calibration flag is open potentially degrading the detector.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Degradation to the detector.

This approach allows more rapid downlink and assessment of the completeness of an accountable data product since all of the instrument science data packets associated with the AID are in a single BDS bin
flight_rule.rationale: The instrument FSW/FW does not enforce a mapping between packets with the same AID to have the same bin ID. Instead, any mapping is enforced by the SIOS team during the command process. So for the instrument to comply with ASRT-150, they need to enforce this FR in ops instead.

Note that whether ASRT-150 is met or not, the science data would still be downloaded and available. However, not complying with ASRT-150 may result in the process of determining whether or not all of the data that was expected as part of an AID more difficult and time consuming.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Spacecraft Agility RCS - Maximum
flight_rule.description: The maximum commanded spacecraft rates and accelerations when under RCS control, in [X, Y, Z], shall be [4.363e-3, 4.363e-3, 4.363e-3] rad/s and [0.750e-3, 0.160e-3, 0.230e-3] rad/s^2, respectively.
flight_rule.rationale:
These are the fastest rates allowable in nominal flight operations (although note that they are not the nominal ones - these fastest rates are fuel inefficient). Using rates faster than these may result in a loss of control and safe mode.
NOTE: During certain spacecraft safe modes, the spacecraft autonomously slews at rates greater than these. The ability to do so is only valid under very specific circumstances with many assumptions. The full agility limitations, with supporting assumptions, are documented in D-103904 (Initial Release).
See associated flight rules: GNC-B-0025, GNC-A-0037, GNC-A-0032
flight_rule.violation_impact: Potential loss of control; trip fault protection and spacecraft safe mode
