related_requirements.requirement: L4 GNC RD: 322961: L4-GNC-Turn time, 180 deg, RCS, fault scenarios

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Spacecraft Agility RWA - Nominal Non-Flyby
flight_rule.description:
When the spacecraft is under RWA control and above 10,000 km in altitude from a celestial body, the maximum commanded spacecraft rates and accelerations shall be, in [X, Y, Z], [1.000e-3, 0.700e-3, 0.700e-3] rad/s and [1.00e-6, 0.80e-6, 0.80e-6] rad/s2 (with the exception of slews commanded only about the X-axis).
See associated flight rules: GNC-A-0005, GNC-A-0004, GNC-A-0032, GNC-A-0037
flight_rule.rationale: Maximum rates and accelerations for any slewing commanded in a general scenario on RWA control. Outside of the closest-approach science time period, the solar arrays could be slewing or tracking the Sun. Therefore, the Y and Z components are smaller than the allowable rates during the closest approach of flybys. The full agility limitations, with supporting assumptions, are documented in D-103904. Celestial bodies include Europa, Callisto, Ganymede, Io, Jupiter, Mars, Earth, and Venus
flight_rule.violation_impact: Potential loss of control; trip fault protection and spacecraft safe mode

reference_info.reference_document: GNC Agility Parameters (D-103904) Initial Release 05/24/2023

related_requirements.requirement: L4 GNC RD: 330345:L4-GNC-Turn rate and accel. capability, RWA

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Spacecraft Agility RWA - Nominal for Flybys (Below 10,000 km)
flight_rule.description:
When the spacecraft is under RWA control and at or below 10,000 km in altitude from a celestial body (implies that the solar arrays are fixed in position) the maximum commanded spacecraft rates and accelerations shall be, in [X, Y, Z], [0.800e-3, 0.900e-3, 0.900e-3] rad/s and [ 0.80e-6, 0.80e-6, 0.80e-6] rad/s2
See associated flight rules: GNC-A-0003, GNC-A-0005, GNC-A-0032, GNC-A-0037
flight_rule.rationale: Maximum rates and accelerations for any slewing commanded during the flyby on RWA control. Note that this is IN ADDITION TO the motion that the body undergoes to track nadir and to fight gravity gradient. During this time, the solar arrays are assumed fixed, which increases the Y and Z components of the rates compared with the non-flyby scenario. However, tracking nadir (with motion primarily about the X-axis) reduces the torque capability available for additional motion about the X-axis, compared with the non-flyby scenario. The full agility limitations, with supporting assumptions, are documented in D-103904. Celestial bodies include Europa, Callisto, Ganymede, Io, Jupiter, Mars, Earth, and Venus.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Potential loss of control; trip fault protection and spacecraft safe mode

reference_info.reference_document: GNC Agility Parameters (D-103904) Initial Release 05/24/2023

related_requirements.requirement: L4 GNC RD: 330345: L4-GNC-Turn rate and accel. capability RWA

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Spacecraft Agility RWA - Nominal for Pure X-axis Rolls Non-Flyby
flight_rule.description:
When the spacecraft is under RWA control, above 10,000 km in altitude from a celestial body, with the solar arrays commanded to a fixed position, and a slew is commanded about the X-axis only, the maximum commanded spacecraft rates and accelerations for that slew shall be, in [X, Y, Z], [1.670e-3, 0.700e-3, 0.700e-3] rad/s and [1.00e-6, 0.80e-6, 0.80e-6] rad/s2, respectively.
See associated flight rules: GNC-A-0003, GNC-A-0004, GNC-A-0032, GNC-A-0037
flight_rule.rationale: This exception to the nominal rates is purely for PIMS and ECM cal rolls. Note that even though a pure X-axis slew is being commanded in this scenario, the commanded Y and Z axis agilities must be non-zero to allow the controller to adjust for minor motions (e.g., motion of celestial bodies that make up the target attitude) in the Y and Z axes. Note that to use these higher rates, the solar arrays must be in a fixed position. The full agility limitations, with supporting assumptions, are documented in D-103904. Celestial bodies include Europa, Callisto, Ganymede, Io, Jupiter, Mars, Earth, and Venus.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Potential loss of control; trip fault protection and spacecraft safe mode

reference_info.reference_document: GNC Agility Parameters (D-103904) Initial Release

related_requirements.requirement: L4 GNC RD: 330345:L4-GNC-Turn rate and accel. capability, RWA

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Spacecraft Solar Array Configuration and Attitude Offset When Under 0.92 AU and in 3J Control
flight_rule.description:
When less than 0.92 AU from the Sun and GNC is in either RCSAcquire3J, pointRCS3J, or pointRCSCelestial control modes, the solar arrays shall be fixed at -41 deg and the spacecraft attitude fixed at an offset of -1.2 deg along the body-frame X-axis from -Y-axis (body-frame) on Sun.
See associated flight rules: GNC-A-0028, GNC-C-0023, GNC-A-0039, GNC-A-0040, PWR-A-0004, PWR-A-0005, GNC-C-0030
flight_rule.rationale:
The fixed solar array position of -41 degrees paired with an X-axis -1.2 deg attitude offset (from -Y on Sun) was determined optimal for preventing the solar arrays from exceeding AFTs when under 0.92 AU while simultaneously keeping the REASON antenna's out of the SRU keep-out-zone. When at distances >0.92 AU, the Sun can remain normal to the solar arrays and the attitude offset (from the -Y on Sun base attitude) set to 0 deg without exceeding AFTs. Note: this flight rule helps to support the thermal restrictions on the Solar Array in inner cruise and still satisfies the attitude constraint set by THRM-A-0004 (-Y-axis shall be within 5 deg of the Sun during inner cruise).
Note: This FR can't be changed or waived without Thermal concurrence.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Risk of violating solar array thermal constraints or entering SRU KOZs.

reference_info.reference_document: MEGA Trajectory SRU-HF Updated Proposal
Risk 918

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Torque Limits on Planned RWA Profile
flight_rule.description:
When using reaction wheels for control, the wheel speed profiles must be planned such that the sum of the profiled torque and gyroscopic torque does not exceed 65 mNm per axis.
See associated flight rule: GNC-B-0038
flight_rule.rationale: These limitations ensure that the planned slewing profile remains within the torque authority of the reaction wheels.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Potentially saturate wheels, resulting in a loss of control

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Spacecraft Y-Axis at Nadir Point
flight_rule.description:
For flybys on RWA control, when at altitudes less than 10,000 km from a celestial body, the SC Y-axis must remain within 7 degrees from nadir crosstrack.
See associated flight rule: GNC-A-0015, GNC-A-0054
flight_rule.rationale: The torque authority of the spacecraft is limited, and in order to track nadir at the close flybys, the gravity gradient torque has to be minimized. Turning the Y-axis further from nadir would increase the gravity gradient torque beyond the torque budget. Said another way, the inertial nadir direction cannot be more than 7 degrees out of the SC YZ plane.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Excessive attitude error; safe mode

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Solar Arrays Parked for Nadir Tracking Flybys
flight_rule.description:
For flybys on RWA control, when the altitude from the targeted celestial body is less than 10,000 km and the spacecraft is nadir tracking the center of that body, the solar arrays must be parked at any fixed articulation angle.
See associated flight rule: GNC-A-0014, GNC-C-0023, GNC-A-0039, GNC-A-0040, GNC-C-0030, PWR-B-0001, REAS-B-0003
flight_rule.rationale: Articulating the solar arrays (including sun track) puts torque on the vehicle, which the reaction wheels need to compensate for. During a flyby, most of the torque capability of the wheels is used up by tracking nadir. Note that this is similar to two other flight rules that exist with different rationales. First, REASON needs a specific angle for their activities (REAS-B-0003). Second, the SADA causes EM interference with REASON, so it must be powered off during the REASON science (PWR-B-0001).
flight_rule.violation_impact: Excessive attitude error; safe mode

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Solar Arrays Parked for Maneuvers
flight_rule.description:
During delta-V burns, the solar arrays must be parked at a fixed articulation angle of either 0 or 180 degrees.
See associated flight rules: GNC-C-0023, GNC-A-0039, GNC-A-0040, GNC-C-0030
flight_rule.rationale: The deltaV controller must be designed to cope with all spacecraft flexibilities one of which is due to the two large solar arrays (as well as other flexibilities such as propellant sloshing). The structural frequencies of the spacecraft depends on the SA articulation angle. The deltaV controller is designed assuming the SA articulation angle is either 0deg or 180 deg . If the arrays are not near either one of these angles, for example, if they are at an angle of 90deg, the Y-axis flexibility becomes driving and its 0.17-Hz mode will have a 70-dB 'spike' greatly reduce the Y-axis bandwidth. Note: the deltaV behavior enforces this constraint, via a parameter that is by default set to 0.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Control goes unstable, loss of attitude control, safe mode

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Enforced by the delta-V behavior
Ensure the parameter is not changed from 0/180

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Ambiguous Turn Axes for 180 deg Slews
flight_rule.description: Slews with a turn angle of greater than 178 degrees shall never be commanded using GNC_ATC_TURN_TO_OFFSET_ABSOLUTE.
flight_rule.rationale: There is ambiguity (i.e., lack of predictability) in the turn axis used by GNC FSW when commanding a near 180 deg slew via GNC_ATC_TURN_TO_OFFSET_ABSOLUTE. If such a slew needs to be commanded, either GNC_ATC_TURN_TO_REL_OFFSET_BASE or GNC_ATC_TO_REL_OFFSET_BODY should be used instead. This rule only applies when the direction of the turn is preferred.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Spacecraft safety is threatened. A slew with an ambiguous turn axis could result in an unexpected violation of Sun constraints, which could cause damage to hardware and/or a spacecraft safing.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: No Simultaneous Solar Array and S/C Slews on Supersafe 3RS
flight_rule.description:
When the spacecraft is using the SuperSafe controller within a 3RS control mode, the solar arrays shall not be articulated while the spacecraft bus is slewing.
See associated flight rules: GNC-C-0023, GNC-A-0037, GNC-A-0040, GNC-C-0030
flight_rule.rationale: Ensures pointing performance of the SuperSafe RCS controller - doing the activities at the same time would result in large attitude control errors
flight_rule.violation_impact: Large attitude control errors - trip fault protection and possibly enter safe mode,

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Manual check of uplink products for the period before going to 3J while in SuperSafe

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Momentum On Transition to RWA Control
flight_rule.description:
The overall system momentum at the moment of transition from RCS to RWA control shall be less than 175 Nms.
See associated flight rules: GNC-A-0055, GNC-B-0030, GNC-B-0052
flight_rule.rationale: A very large momentum at the moment of transition could overload the wheels and lead to excessive attitude error or excessive momentum. This assumes momentum knowledge error of no more than 25 Nms.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Safe mode

reference_info.reference_document: L4 GNC RD: 333449: L4-GNC-Rates for RCS to RWA transition

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: SRU Usage in Celestial Modes
flight_rule.description:
Before a commanded transition to a Celestial mode (PointRCSCelestial, PointRWACelestial, or ControlIdleCelestial), and during the entirety of the duration spent in a Celestial mode, both SRU heads must be powered on and the GNC must be commanded to be using both heads in the attitude estimate.
See associated flight rules: GNC-A-0033, GNC-A-0032, GNC-B-0027, GNC-A-0050
flight_rule.rationale:
The GNC Celestial modes rely upon only the SRUs for attitude knowledge (no IMU). As such, the fault response to a loss of all SRU data while in these modes is quick and severe (3R safe mode). Having two heads powered on reduces the likelihood of both heads being obscured, or otherwise not producing data, while in these Celestial modes.
If it is not possible to have both OH heads powered on and configured in ATE (and this Flight Rule fails), then it is required to ensure no bright body obscurations on the single SRU head during Celestial mode.
flight_rule.violation_impact: In the event of an SRU obscuration, 3R safe mode (Sun search)

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Celestial Mode Only in Low Radiation
flight_rule.description:
GNC shall not be in a Celestial mode (PointRCSCelestial, PointRWACelestial, or ControlIdleCelestial) when the spacecraft is <= 15Rj from Jupiter's center.
See associated flight rules: GNC-A-0030, GNC-A-0032, GNC-A-0033, GNC-B-0044, GNC-A-050
flight_rule.rationale: 'Low-radiation regime' is defined for this flight rule by a distance from Jupiter's center greater than 15Rj. The GNC Celestial modes rely upon only the SRUs for attitude knowledge (no IMU). As such, the fault response to a loss of all SRU data while in these modes is quick and severe (3R safe mode). Though the SRUs are expected to track stars through the expected radiation environment, they are not guaranteed to be able to re-gain inertial knowledge in the high radiation regime if it does lose tracking - which would result in no SRU data.
flight_rule.violation_impact: In the event of an SRU obscuration or radiation drop-out, 3R safe mode (Sun search)

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Spacecraft Agility - Celestial
flight_rule.description:
When GNC is in a Celestial mode (PointRCSCelestial, PointRWACelestial, or ControlIdleCelestial), the maximum commanded spacecraft rates and accelerations are, in [X, Y, Z], [2.181e-3, 2.181e-3, 2.181e-3] rad/s and [0.750e-3, 0.160e-3, 0.230e-3] rad/s2
See associated flight rules: GNC-A-0004, GNC-A-0003, GNC-B-0025, GNC-A-0001, GNC-A-0037, GNC-A-0005, GNC-A-0030
flight_rule.rationale: The GNC Celestial modes rely upon only the SRUs for attitude knowledge (no IMU). As such, the fault response to a loss of all SRU data while in these modes is quick and severe (3R safe mode). In order for the SRUs to be able to track stars, the spacecraft rates and acceleration must remain sufficiently small.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Will go into 3R safe mode (Sun search).

reference_info.reference_document: GNC Agility Parameters (D-103904) Initial Release 05/24/2023

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: David Tong to specify.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Spacecraft Agility RCS Supersafe with Unknown Inertias
flight_rule.description:
While GNC is configured to the RCS SuperSafe controller, prior to the post-Launch GNC parameter update that updates GNC_EXC_DEPLOYED_CONFIG to ACS_CTL_GNC_DEPLOYED, the maximum commanded rates and accelerations of the spacecraft in [X,Y,Z] shall be limited to [1.745e-03, 1.745e-03, 1.745e-03] rad/s and [0.050e-03, 0.050-03, 0.050e-03] rad/s^2 respectively.
See associated flight rules: GNC-A-0027, GNC-A-0004, GNC-A-0003, GNC-A-0032, GNC-B-0025, GNC-A-0001, GNC-A-0005
flight_rule.rationale: Prior to updating GNC_EXC_DEPLOYED_CONFIG to ACS_CTL_GNC_DEPLOYED, GNC algorithms assume the spacecraft moment-of-inertias are unknown. This is intended to provide robustness to the off-nominal case where one or both solar arrays do not fully deploy during the Launch Behavior. While the moment-of-inertias are effectively unknown, greater operation caution is required to keep the spacecraft within the validated constraints of the RCS SuperSafe controller, which envelopes all possible deployment configurations.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Potential loss of control; trip fault protection and spacecraft safe mode

reference_info.reference_document: GNC Agility Parameters (D-103904) Initial Release 05/24/2023

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: manual check

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: No RWA control until after the post-FreqID#2 GNC parameter update
flight_rule.description:
GNC shall not enter the PointRWA3J and PointRWACelestial control mode until after the GNC parameter update following Frequency-ID #2 that transitions the RCS and RWA controllers from the launch to nominal gain settings is completed.
See associated flight rules: GNC-A-0045, GNC-A-0049
flight_rule.rationale: GNC launches configured to the SuperSafe RCS controller, which is the only pre-loaded onboard attitude controller that is robust to the uncertainty in the spacecraft flex dynamics. GNC will perform two Frequency-ID activities at the start of the mission (the first following solar array deployment, and the second following the deployment of the REASON antennas and ECM magboom) to verify/identify the major flexible modes of the spacecraft. Following the second of these activities, GNC will use the collected data to update the RCS and RWA controller gains from their at-launch values (i.e. SuperSafe for RCS) to their nominal, high-performance settings. Prior to this GNC parameter update, use of the RWA controller (by transitioning to the control mode PointRWA3J or PointRWACelestial) could result in unexpected flex mode excitations/unstable controller behavior and or damage to hardware.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Potential for unstable spacecraft control, damage to hardware, and in the worst case, loss of vehicle.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Enforced via GNC Ops procedures

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Solar Array Command on Transition to Coast/Control Idle
flight_rule.description:
Prior to a ground commanded entry into a Control Idle or Coast mode, the Solar Array commander should be commanded to point the arrays at a fixed (non-sun-tracking) position.
See associated flight rules: GNC-A-0015, GNC-C-0030, GNC-A-0010, GNC-A-0016
flight_rule.rationale: SAC uses the commanded attitude to determine where the sun is supposed to be in the body frame, but since there is no commanded attitude when we are in a Control Idle (ControlIdleAcq3R, ControlIdle3R, ControlIdle3RS, ControlIdleAcq3J, ControlIdle3J, or ControlIdleCelestial) or Coast (Coast3J, or CoastCel) mode, the commanded sun vector used by SAC will be invalid.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Fault protection; undervoltage

enforcement_method.enforcement_description:
DT 09/03/21 ControlIdleAcq3R does not exist in FSW R8, this is not a valid for GNC_ACS_CTL_MODES.
DT 09/03/21 SEQGen will monitor the command GNC_ACS_CHANGE_MODE, if the command parameter is one of these values: GNC_ACS_CTLIDLE_3R, GNC_ACS_CTLIDLE_3RS, GNC_ACS_CTLIDLE_ACQ_3J, GNC_ACS_CTLIDLE_3J, GNC_ACS_CTLIDLE_CEL, GNC_ACS_COAST_3J, GNC_ACS_COAST_CEL SAC need to point to a non-sun-tracking position (not sure how to check this)
Should be checkable by merlin and seqgen.
If it is determined that this FR should be implemented in Merlin, here is a potential FOL that can be used to implement it. This FOL description references states, and enforcement will be at the activity planning level in Merlin. (The temporal logic is contained in the derived state in this case.)
FOL Descriptions: [(before_sc_control_idle_mode = TRUE) OR (before_sc_control_coast_mode = TRUE)] AND (SA_position_fixed_non_sun_tracking = TRUE)
FOL Evaluation Description: List of Windows that contain the times before changing to one of the specified modes that the SA is not at a fixed non-sun-tracking position. Any Windows that are returned are in VIOLATION.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: No Mode Change During SA Articulation
flight_rule.description: Do not command a GNC control mode change during a planned solar array (SA) articulation.
flight_rule.rationale:
SAC enforces mode dependent rate and acceleration limits but only receives updates to those limits when it receives a new articulation command. If an articulation using RCS control were to be on-going during a transition to RWA control then it is possible that the articulation could exceed the RWA torque availability to reject the disturbance.
See associated flight rules: GNC-A-0010, GNC-A-0015, GNC-A-0016, GNC-C-0030, GNC-C-0023, GNC-A-0027
flight_rule.violation_impact: Fault protection; trip excessive attitude or rate error

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Limit Updates of DeltaH and DeltaV Vectors
flight_rule.description:
The DeltaH and DeltaV vectors shall not be directly updated by the ground in the Ephemeris Management Table.
See associated flight rule: GNC-A-0026
flight_rule.rationale:
Nominally, these vectors will be updated by the Motion Behavior Manager (MBM), in the process of executing the DO_MOMENTUM_MANAGEMENT or DO_DELTAV behaviors. The only time that the ground should need to update these vectors directly is if a ground sequence is replacing one of the MBM behaviors. This flight rule will protect against conflicts between ground updates and MBM updates.
Note: if the update is part of a ground sequence of a RWA bias or a deltaV burn, then a waiver would be required. Otherwise, DO_MOMENTUM_MANAGEMENT and DO_DELTAV will manage these vectors.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Momentum bias or DeltaV burn execute in the wrong direction, costing propellant and deltaV

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: SET will ensure dV and dH vectors will not be updated unless overwritten (which would require a waiver of this FR). Reference SET requirement 1003293.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: SRU Power Cycling
flight_rule.description: After an SRU electronics unit is commanded to be powered off, at least 10 seconds must pass before the command to power-on is sent
flight_rule.rationale: Testing on the Simulator showed that the device locked up and was unresponsive (if powered off and on again too quickly)
flight_rule.violation_impact: SRU hardware fault, leading to hardware swapping or system safe mode

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Control Idle state during ECM boom and REASON deployments
flight_rule.description: GNC shall be commanded to a Control Idle mode (ControlIdleAcq3R, ControlIdle3R, ControlIdle3RS, ControlIdleAcq3J, ControlIdle3J, or ControlIdleCelestial) for the duration of the ECM boom and REASON HF and VHF antenna deployments. See associated flight rules: GNC-A-0038, GNC-C-0029, GNC-A-0048.
flight_rule.rationale: The ECM boom and REASON antenna deployments will impart dynamic signatures on the system that are detectable by the IMU. Since these signatures are unmodeled, the resulting controller response is unknown and thus unverified.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Potential loss of control; trip fault protection and spacecraft safe mode and/or damage to hardware.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Manual check of the deployment sequences.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Control Idle/Coast to RWA Control Mode Transitions
flight_rule.description:
When in a Control Idle or Coast mode, GNC shall not directly transition to RWA control if the previous mode was an RCS control mode.
See associated flight rule: GNC-C-0029, GNC-C-0028, GNC-A-0052, GNC-A-0045, GNC-A-0012
flight_rule.rationale: If GNC was in an RCS control mode prior to entering either Control Idle or Coast (i.e. ControlIdleAcq3R, ControlIdle3R, ControlIdle3RS, ControlIdleAcq3J, ControlIdle3J, ControlIdleCelestial, Coast3J, or CoastCel), the spacecraft body rates may be too high for RWA control to overcome, which could lead to loss of control of the spacecraft. To prevent this scenario, GNC must first transition back to RCS control prior to entering RWA control. Although Motion behavior commands are listed in this flight rule, they have been designed to autonomously make the appropriate transition from idle/coast modes.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Potential loss of control of the spacecraft; trip fault protection and spacecraft safe mode and/or damage to hardware.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: No 3J Control Modes Prior to Solar Array Deployment
flight_rule.description:
GNC shall not command the first transition from RCSTrkSunPoint to RCSAcquire3J until success of solar array deployment has been confirmed by the ground.
See associated flight rules: GNC-A-0038
flight_rule.rationale: The SuperSafe controller will be active at this time (i.e., from launch until after a parameter update following Frequency-ID #2). Entering pointRCS3J while on the SuperSafe controller, following a successful autonomous transition out of RCSAcquire3J, unlocks capabilities (such as faster agilities) that have not been verified for any spacecraft configuration preceding full solar array deployment. Use of any these functionalities prior to this event could result in unexpected/unstable controller behavior and/or damage to hardware.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Potential for unstable spacecraft control, damage to hardware, and, in the worst case, loss of vehicle.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description:
Procedural check by GNC ops team.
Note (W. Sanchez 9/2021): While no telemetry channel exists to report the deployed state of the solar arrays, GNC Ops will be cognizant of the deployed state (and will be updating the parameter GNC_EXC_DEPLOYED_CONFIG).

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: No IMU Swaps in IMU Control Modes
flight_rule.description:
Changing prime IMU configuration (to IMU-A or IMU-B) shall be performed only in modes where IMU measurements are not used in closed-loop control: RESET, PointRCSCelestial, PointRWACelestial, ControlIdleCelestial, and CoastCel.
See associated flight rules: GNC-B-0028, GNC-A-0033, GNC-A-0031, GNC-A-0030
flight_rule.rationale: Swapping IMU primeness could lead to a momentary discontinuity in inertial data received by the sensor. To prevent a potential safing response (as directed by ECR-20485), this activity should only be performed in control modes where GNC is not actively using IMU measurements in closed-loop control (RESET, PointRCSCelestial, PointRWACelestial, ControlIdleCelestial, or CoastCel).
flight_rule.violation_impact: Potential loss of control; trip fault protection and spacecraft safe mode

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: GNC Parameter Set and Load Commands Must Not Overlap
flight_rule.description:
The execution of GNC_ACS_LOAD_PARAMS shall not overlap with the execution of any parameter update commands (DDM_BEGIN_TRANS_SYS_PARAM, DDM_END_TRANS_SYS_PARAM, DDM_FILE_SET_SYS_PARAM, DDM_RESTORE_SYS_PARAM, DDM_RESTORE_SYS_PARAM_IND, DDM_SET_SYS_PARAM_FLT, DDM_SET_SYS_PARAM_I16, DDM_SET_SYS_PARAM_I8, DDM_SET_SYS_PARAM_STR, DDM_SET_SYS_PARAM_U16, DDM_SET_SYS_PARAM_U8,DDM_SET_SYS_PARAM_U32, and DDM_SET_SYS_PARAM_I32)
See associated flight rules: GNC-C-0026, GNC-A-0046, GNC-C-0028, GNC-A-0041
flight_rule.rationale:
The commands that place new values for parameters into the volatile memory parameter database (i.e., DDM_BEGIN_TRANS_SYS_PARAM, DDM_END_TRANS_SYS_PARAM, DDM_FILE_SET_SYS_PARAM, DDM_RESTORE_SYS_PARAM, DDM_RESTORE_SYS_PARAM_IND, DDM_SET_SYS_PARAM_FLT, DDM_SET_SYS_PARAM_I16, DDM_SET_SYS_PARAM_I8, DDM_SET_SYS_PARAM_STR, DDM_SET_SYS_PARAM_U16, DDM_SET_SYS_PARAM_U8,DDM_SET_SYS_PARAM_U32, and DDM_SET_SYS_PARAM_I32.) and the command that loads those new values into the inactive GNC parameter buffer (GNC_ACS_LOAD_PARAMS) do not mutually exclude each other. As such, simultaneous execution of both kinds of commands could cause a "mixed bag" condition, where a subset of new parameter values are loaded alongside a subset of old parameter values.
Under this condition, a subsequent GNC_ACS_SWAP_PARAMS command would cause the mixed bag of parameters to become active. The resulting controller response would be unknown and thus unverified. Because these commands (especially GNC_ACS_LOAD_PARAMS) can take an indeterminate amount of time to complete, it is not sufficient to schedule exclusions based on timing. One command must be verified as completed before another can begin.
The command completion dependencies that enforce this constraint shall be verified either on the ground using command telemetry or through the use of event-driven sequencing.
flight_rule.violation_impact: If a mixed bag of GNC parameters were made active, it could potentially lead to loss of control, safing, or damage to the spacecraft hardware.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: SAC Hard Initialization in Control Idle
flight_rule.description:
Planned hard initializations of the SADA articulation angle shall be performed while in a GNC Control Idle mode (ControlIdleAcq3R, ControlIdle3R, ControlIdle3RS, ControlIdleAcq3J, ControlIdle3J, or ControlIdleCelestial).
See associated flight rules: GNC-B-0062, GNC-A-0048, GNC-C-0029
flight_rule.rationale: Hard Initializations, where the arrays are driven into the hard stop at high rate will result in large transients in spacecraft rate and acceleration, which the RCS controller could respond to harshly with significant engine firing. Though the disturbance from the hard initialization has not received detailed dynamic simulation, it is anticipated that RCS control transients will be large enough to violate geometric constraints. Furthermore, if on RWA control, it is anticipated that the disturbances could lead to loss-of-control of the spacecraft.
flight_rule.violation_impact: At best, unexpected deltaV and propellant usage; pointing degradation. Potentially spacecraft safing or loss-of-control.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Primary and Secondary Inertial Target Vector Separation
flight_rule.description:
When defining a base attitude in a 3J pointing control mode, the angle between the Primary Inertial Target Vector and the Secondary Inertial Target Vector shall not be within 5 degrees of being aligned or **anti-aligned** throughout the range of time the vectors are used.
See associated flight rule: GNC-B-0059
flight_rule.rationale: This constraint avoids a singularity that occurs when the primary and secondary inertial target vectors become parallel (aligned) or anti-parallel (anti-aligned), which can then trigger an unplanned large angle (180 deg or 360 deg) slew.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Unexpected propellant usage, loss of target, which could potentially lead to thermal and dynamic stability issues, etc.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: No Desats During Flyby
flight_rule.description:
During Jupiter tour the spacecraft shall not perform momentum wheel desaturations between the data cutoff for the approach maneuver and the end of the associated Nadir phase.
See associated flight rule: GNC-A-0014
flight_rule.rationale: Performing desats immediately prior to a flyby will impact the accuracy of the navigation prediction and delivery to target. At worst, if the activity imparts a delta-V on the spacecraft (with a large enough magnitude), the spacecraft could be put on an impact trajectory with Europa.
flight_rule.violation_impact: At best, this may affect the accuracy of the flyby altitude/trajectory and have a potential damage to mission return. At worst, impact with Europa and loss-of-spacecraft/end-of-mission.

related_requirements.requirement: L2-PSRD 673349: No Desats During Flybys L3-SCRD 330376: No Desats During Flybys L4-GNC 333450: No desat's during flyby

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Settling Time Before Transition from RCS to RWA
flight_rule.description:
When the spacecraft is under RCS control, there must be at least 15 minutes of quiescent time before a transition to RWA control.
See associated flight rules: GNC-B-0052, GNC-B-0049, GNC-B-0032, GNC-B-0047, GNC-B-0031, GNC-A-0029, GNC-B-0050
flight_rule.rationale: Quiescent time is defined as body rates in [X, Y, Z] being below [0.436, 0.175, 0.175] mrad/sec. The spacecraft has more control authority under RCS control, and so the agility parameters are larger than RWA control. The resulting dynamics of the spacecraft could be outside the performance capability of the RWA controller, which could trip fault protection monitors and lead to spacecraft safing. In addition, the ground-predicted wheel rates are dependent on the spacecraft rate uncertainty at the moment of transition from RCS to RWA. If the spacecraft rates are higher due to dynamics, that will greatly increase the uncertainty in wheel rate predictions.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Degraded pointing performance; large error in predicted wheel speeds. Potential for spacecraft safing.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: The DO-PointRWA3J behavior enforces a wait time (it actually waits for a notification from GNC) before the transition from RCS to RWA.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Wait Time Between Wheel Config Change and Momentum Management Behavior
flight_rule.description:
If an RWA has been powered off, do not execute the momentum management behavior unless either EHA can be used to confirm that the wheel has fully spun down, or at least 17.1 hours have passed.
See associated flight rules: GNC-B-0038, GNC-A-0008
flight_rule.rationale: In the execution of a wheel configuration change, a wheel can be left spinning with power off and wheel speed unmeasurable, leaving the knowledge error of system momentum large. Following a power off, it can take up to 17.1 hours for a reaction wheel to fully spin down. Note: the 17.1 hour estimate assumes a constant drag torque of 0.005 Nm and includes an uncertainty factor of 2.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Excessive momentum could lead to tripping of spacecraft safe mode.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: DT 09/27/2021 SEQGen will set an attribute "ALLOW_MOM_MGNT" state to false and reset it to true after 17.1 hours. SEQGen will check this attribute when GNC_MBM_DO_MOM_MGMT is executed. SEQGen will not able to check the EHA for fully spun down condition.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: RCS Control for Gravity Assists
flight_rule.description:
GNC must be on RCS control while below an altitude of 10,000km for the Earth, Mars, and Ganymede (G0) gravity assists.
See associated flight rule: GNC-B-0059
flight_rule.rationale:
The spacecraft will experience gravity gradient and atmospheric torques while passing through closest approach of the Earth, Mars, and Ganymede gravity assists. It is unverified if the RWA control system can reject these disturbances and maintain the inertially fixed attitude prescribed for the flybys.
Note this applies only to the G0 Ganymede gravity assist flyby, not the flybys during tour.
May possibly apply for gravity assists to achieve de-orbit.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Potential loss of control, spacecraft safe mode.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Avoid Overusing SADAs
flight_rule.description: Do not power either SADA more than 200 minutes cumulatively across any moving 8-hour window.
flight_rule.rationale:
Each SADA self-heats while powered on and can overheat (specifically, the SADA potentiometers may exceed maximum allowable flight temperature (AFT)) if the SADA is powered on for long periods continuously or for significant percentage of time over a given period.
Limiting nominal operations below stated limits ensures SADA max AFTs will not be violated during normal operations and the SADA can safely sustain further operation supporting safing behaviors without exceeding protoflight (PFT) limits. Exceeding AFT (but not PFT) will not immediately damage the SADA, but failing to limit nominal operations below AFT would leave insufficient headroom to support off-nominal safing responses.
Key SADA temperatures are not actively monitored/mitigated onboard. Flight System instead relies solely on this planning constraint to avoid overheating the SADAs.
Current values in this rule are based on preliminary modeling prior to launch. This rule may be modified upon refinement of thermal modeling and/or margin, including updates driven by analysis of flight data from the SADA potentiometer PRTs.
flight_rule.violation_impact: SADA temperature may exceed max AFT, leaving insufficient headroom to safely support safing operations.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Independent Solar Array Articulations While on SuperSafe RCS
flight_rule.description: The commanded Positive X (PX) and Negative X (MX) solar array angles shall never differ by more than 5 degrees while GNC is configured to the SuperSafe RCS controller.
flight_rule.rationale: Independent solar array articulations with commanded angles that differ in excess of what may be required by the SADA Checkout activity of FSC1 (i.e., 5 degrees) was neither scoped in the design of the SuperSafe RCS controller nor verified for controllability while under its configuration. Thus, the resulting controller response to these large asymmetric motions is unknown-which could include spacecraft safing/loss of control if violated.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Potential loss of control; trip fault protection and spacecraft safe mode and/or damage to hardware.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Manual check of uplink products for the period before going to 3J while in SuperSafe

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Spacecraft Solar Array Configuration and Attitude Offset When Under 0.92 AU and 3RS Control
flight_rule.description: When the spacecraft is less than 0.92 AU from the Sun, fixed-pointed with the body-frame -Y-axis toward the Sun, and GNC is in RCSTrkSunPoint control mode, the solar arrays shall be fixed at an articulation angle between -42.2 and -90 degrees.
flight_rule.rationale: The fixed solar array position between -90 deg and -42.2 deg was determined optimal for preventing the solar arrays from exceeding AFTs when under 0.92 AU. Unlike GNC-A-0010, in this case GNC is in 3RS (non-SRU) control. Thus, special care does not need to be taken to keep the REASON antenna's out of the SRU keep-out-zone, which permits for a greater range of allowable SA articulation angles. When at distances >0.92 AU, the Sun can remain normal to the solar arrays without exceeding AFTs. Note: this flight rule helps to support the thermal restrictions on the Solar Array in inner cruise (see THRM-A-0005).
flight_rule.violation_impact: Risk of violating solar array thermal constraints leading to reduced power generation capability.

reference_info.reference_document: Inner Cruise Solar Array Angle

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Contingency procedure enforcement

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: No RWA Config Changes in RWA Control Modes
flight_rule.description: The RWA wheel configuration shall not be changed while GNC is in an RWA active control mode (pointRWA3J, pointRWACelestial).
flight_rule.rationale: MOS can select which reaction wheels to use within closed-loop RWA control by updating the System FSW parameter GNC_RWA_FOR_GNC_CONTROL_SELECTION. Changing the wheel configuration while in an RWA active control mode will create a wheel speed profile discontinuity that can easily trip several RWA related FP monitors such as RWA speed control error (MON_GNC_RTA_SPD_CTRL_ERR_RWA_X) and safe the vehicle. Therefore, updates of this System parameter should occur outside of an RWA-based control mode. NOTE: GNC recommends performing the switch in ControlIdle3J or ControlIdleCelestial to avoid unnecessary propellant expenditure or residual delta-V.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Trip an RWA FP monitor and safe the spacecraft.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description:
SEQGen can partially check this flight rule when the parameter "GNC_RWA_FOR_GNC_CONTROL_SELECTION" is being updated from a command. Manual check is needed when this parameter is being updated from a file.
SEQGen will monitor the "DDM_SET_SYS_PARAM_STR" command and its param_id. If the param_id = ="0x0A120014", "GNC_RWA_FOR_GNC_CONTROL_SELECTION" and the GNC attribute ACS_MODE is either "GNC_ACS_POINTRWA_3J" or "GNC_ACS_POINTRWA_CEL", SEQGen will flag an error.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: The DEFAULT_HOLD Body Vectors Set Only to Protected Body Frame Vectors
flight_rule.description: The parameters GNC_ATC_DEF_PRI_BODY_VEC_NAME_0 GNC_ATC_DEF_SEC_BODY_VEC_NAME_0, that together define the primary and secondary body vectors of the default 3J attitude GNC_DEFAULT_HOLD, shall each be set to one of the following six protected VCS body frame vectors, which can not be the same vector for both: GNC_VCS_POS_X_AXIS_BF GNC_VCS_POS_Y_AXIS_BF GNC_VCS_POS_Z_AXIS_BF GNC_VCS_NEG_X_AXIS_BF GNC_VCS_NEG_Y_AXIS_BF GNC_VCS_NEG_Z_AXIS_BF
flight_rule.rationale:
The parameters GNC_ATC_DEF_PRI_BODY_VEC_NAME_0 and GNC_ATC_DEF_SEC_BODY_VEC_NAME_0 together define the primary and secondary body vectors for the default 3J attitude type GNC_DEFAULT_HOLD. In practice, the parameters can take any value in the enumeration GNC_VCS_BODY_VEC_NAME_T. However, the ground should restrict the admissible values to the six protected vectors aligned with the +/- X, +/- Y, +/-Z spacecraft body frame axes.
Fault Protection uses the GNC_DEFAULT_HOLD attitude when autonomously passing out of Detumble through Acquire3J. Using an unprotected vector (that is, one that can be modified in flight) leaves the spacecraft vulnerable to an unexpected final attitude once 3J control is reached---which can lead to sun exposure violations, uploss, additional safings etc.
GNC_ATC_DEF_PRI_BODY_VEC_NAME_0 and GNC_ATC_DEF_SEC_BODY_VEC_NAME_0 should not be set to the same body frame vector as it results in undefined pointing.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Unexpected final attitude, at worst sun exposure violations, uploss, safing.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Solar array angle in SuperSafe control
flight_rule.description: While in SuperSafe control, the commanded solar array angle for either the +X or -X wing must remain in the range between -45 deg and +45 deg.
flight_rule.rationale: Due to a limitation of available Finite Element Models for this phase of the mission where the spacecraft configuration is changing a lot, the SupersafeRCS controller was unable to be V&Ved for the full range of solar array angles. Note that this restriction is inherit in the controller design, and will still apply even with the unlocked agilities.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Possible controller instability and RCS safing.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Transitions to Control Idle Include Commands to Return to Control
flight_rule.description: Any commanded transition to an uncontrolled GNC sub-mode (ControlIdleAcq3R, ControlIdle3R, ControlIdle3RS, ControlIdleAcq3J, ControlIdle3J, ControlIdleCelestial, Coast3J, CoastCel, Reset) must be part of a sequence that includes a command to return to active attitude control later in the same sequence
flight_rule.rationale: Commanding the SC to an uncontrolled GNC sub-mode could result in the SC drifting to an attitude where uplink is lost (that is, the spacecraft is not commandable). In this scenario, there would be no timeout or autonomous response that could return the SC back to an active attitude control mode. Sequences that take us to uncontrolled GNC modes are only safe if they include the command to go back to an active attitude control mode at their conclusion. In the event that a fault response terminates the active sequence, FP has confirmed that all fault responses that kill sequences will enforce a GNC attitude as part of the response.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Potential loss of spacecraft.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Spacecraft Agility RCS SuperSafe with Known Inertias
flight_rule.description: While GNC is configured to the RCS SuperSafe controller, following the post-Launch GNC parameter update that includes update of the parameter GNC_EXC_DEPLOYED_CONFIG to ACS_CTL_GNC_DEPLOYED, the maximum commanded rates and accelerations of the spacecraft in [X,Y,Z] shall be limited to [4.363e-03, 4.363e-03, 4.363-03] rad/s and [0.050e-03, 0.050-03, 0.050e-03] rad/s^2 respectively.
flight_rule.rationale:
Updating the parameter GNC_EXC_DEPLOYED_CONFIG to ACS_CTL_GNC_DEPLOYED provides confirmation to GNC algorithms that both solar arrays have successfully deployed, indicating that the moment-of-inertias of the spacecraft are now effectively known. This action unlocks higher rate limits, which may be needed to meet off-Sun pointing time requirements in the early phases of the mission. Note: the lower (i.e., than the nominal RCS controller) accelerations are still enforced in order to prevent exceeding the capability of the low-bandwidth RCS SuperSafe controller.
NOTE 1: The post-Launch parameter update will also update CMT inertial rate/accel limit parameters and FP threshholds to be commensurate with the higher allowed rates.
NOTE 2: This is opposed to the unknown inertia case that guards against a partial or failed solar array deployment (see GNC-A-0037)
flight_rule.violation_impact: Potential loss of control; trip fault protection and spacecraft safe mode.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Spacecraft Agility RCS - Nominal
flight_rule.description:
When the spacecraft is at or above 2 AU from the Sun and under RCS control, the maximum commanded spacecraft rates and accelerations, in [X, Y, Z], should be [2.18, 2.18, 2.18] mrad/s and [1.0e-3, 0.26e-3 0.28e-3] rad/s2, respectively.
See associated flight rules: GNC-A-0037, GNC-A-0032, GNC-A-0001
flight_rule.rationale: The propellant budget pre-launch assumes that these rates are used nominally at all times when the spacecraft is at or above 2 AU from the Sun. It is possible to increase the rates at the inadvisable cost of propellant consumption. Note that these rates apply to a deployed configuration.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Unexpected propellant cost and deltaV

enforcement_method.enforcement_description:

FOL Evaluation Description: List of Windows that contain the times the S/C is in RCS mode and at or above 2AU from the Sun and the max rate or acceleration exceed the limit. Any Windows that are returned are in VIOLATION.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Accelerometer On for Maneuvers
flight_rule.description:
During engine maneuvers, the prime accelerometer must be powered on.
See associated flight rules: GNC-B-0056, GNC-B-0037
flight_rule.rationale: For the critical JOI deltaV burn, both IMUs will be powered on. One IMU will be designated prime and the other IMU is a 'hot' backup. For non-critical deltaV burns, only one of the two IMUs (the one that is designated prime) will be powered on. The accelerometers of the prime IMU will be used to estimate the S/C's Z-axis deltaV. Burn will be cutoff when the commanded deltaV has been achieved. Without a functional ACC from either IMU-A or IMU-B, GNC could only rely on a virtual accelerometer.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Degraded maneuver performance in magnitude accuracy - it is a design choice if the maneuver completes based on the model

reference_info.reference_document: L4 GNC RD: 1037949: L4-GNC-Delta-V accuracy

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: DSS Calibration Frequency
flight_rule.description:
Each Digital Sun Sensors shall be calibrated at least every 12 months.
See associated flight rules: GNC-C-0025, GNC-B-0060, GNC-B-0044, GNC-B-0043, GNC-B-0042
flight_rule.rationale: The Digital Sun Sensors (DSSs) are expected to degrade over time due to radiation effects. It is important to track this information and make any necessary adjustments to the on-board parameters based on the calibrations
flight_rule.violation_impact: Degradation in Sun sensor accuracy

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: RWA Characterization Frequency
flight_rule.description:
Each reaction wheel assembly shall be characterized at least every 12 months.
See associated flight rules: GNC-A-0029, GNC-C-0021, GNC-C-0025, GNC-B-0060, GNC-B-0042
flight_rule.rationale: In absence of 1g environment, grease is not expected to "slump" or require additional run-in to distribute grease; however, it is beneficial to re-establish grease channels periodically to ensure anomalous behavior is avoided. 60 months is allowed ground (1g) storage prior to requiring run-in to re-establish grease channels. Best characterization is a coastdown test but expensive for fuel to do during mission. Possibly just operate in mode with all 4 RWAs being used for control for the day (this could be accomplished in conjunction with Guideline #35 - Prime Set Rotation). Note: this activity may also be named RWA Drag Torque Calibration.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Possible grease redistribution event (momentary high drag due to re-creating grease channels)

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Accelerometer Bias Calibrations After RWA Biases
flight_rule.description:
An accelerometer bias calibration must be performed after every unbalanced reaction wheel bias, and must be completed no later than 5 minutes after the transition back to RWA control.
See associated flight rules: GNC-B-0037, GNC-B-0035, GNC-A-0008
flight_rule.rationale:
Most RWA biases are performed with Y-facing (coupled) engines by slewing to align the spacecraft Z-axis with the delta-momentum vector (i.e. 'balanced biases'). The reconstruction of the small deltaV due to biasing could be estimated using the estimated S/C's mass and the engine impulse-EPW model. However, RWA biasing that are performed using both Y and Z-facing engines (i.e. 'unbalanced biases') will generate larger deltaV that must be reconstructed using the accelerometer data. To this end, the ACC bias must be calibrated. To achieve a high level of deltaV reconstruction accuracy, ACC bias must be calibrated before and after the RWA biasing.
Note that this flight rule will be met automatically if the Momentum Management behavior is used.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Poor deltaV reconstruction accuracy (leads to inaccuracies in OD)

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Verify use of MM behavior

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Accelerometer Bias Calibrations Before RWA Biases
flight_rule.description:
The accelerometer bias calibration must be performed before every unbalanced reaction wheel bias, and must be completed at most 5 minutes before the transition to RCS control.
See associated flight rules: GNC-B-0034, GNC-B-0037, GNC-A-0008
flight_rule.rationale:
Most RWA biases are performed with Y-facing (coupled) engines by slewing to align the spacecraft Z-axis with the delta-momentum vector (i.e. 'balanced biases'). The reconstruction of the small deltaV due to biasing could be estimated using the estimated S/C's mass and the engine impulse-EPW model. However, RWA biasing that are performed using both Y and Z-facing engines (i.e. 'non-balanced biases') will generate larger deltaV that must be reconstructed using the accelerometer data. To this end, the ACC bias must be calibrated. To achieve a high level of deltaV reconstruction accuracy, ACC bias must be calibrated before and after the RWA biasing.
Note that this flight rule will be met automatically if the Momentum Management behavior is used.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Poor deltaV reconstruction accuracy (leads to inaccuracies in OD)

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Verify use of MM behavior

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Accelerometer Bias Calibrations for Maneuvers
flight_rule.description:
The accelerometer bias calibration must be performed before every engine maneuver, and completed within 10 minutes of burn ignition.
See associated flight rules: GNC-B-0035, GNC-B-0034, GNC-B-0026, GNC-B-0056
flight_rule.rationale: The accelerometers are used for cutting off burns. The Gates budget assumes a drift of 15 min. Without a "fresh" ACC bias calibration performed just before ignition, the FSW will use an old ACC bias value which might deviate from the "truth". This is enforced by the do_deltaV behavior.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Degraded maneuver performance in (proportional) magnitude accuracy

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Enforced by do_deltaV behavior.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: No SRU Obscurations During IMU Calibrations
flight_rule.description: Do not allow SRU obscurations during an IMU calibration.
flight_rule.rationale:
An IMU calibration requires SRU telemetry throughout the entire activity. An SRU obscuration would prevent SRU telemetry and therefore cause the calibration during that time to be meaningless.
See associated flight rules: GNC-B-0045, GNC-C-0024, GNC-B-0060, GNC-B-0053, GNC-B-0086, GNC-A-0033
flight_rule.violation_impact: IMU calibration is unsuccessful, and could result in degraded science pointing for the following flyby

enforcement_method.enforcement_description:
Sloan talk w/Phil Good or Todd Brown.
Will also reference the Shaun Johnson obscuration memo.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Settling Time before Engine Maneuver Ignition
flight_rule.description: The commanded start time of the burn shall be at least 15 minutes after the end of last completed slew
flight_rule.rationale: Spacecraft turns shall excite the propellants in the large bipropellant tank assemblies to move relative to the tank walls. Turns will also excite the solar array modes. A waiting period of at least 15 minutes is necessary after the S/C turn completion before operating the engines to provide sufficient time for the propellant management devices to stabilize the bipropellants in each tank and for the solar array motion to dampen. This is a parameter in the maneuver behavior. The adequacy of the selected 15-min settling time should be confirmed inflight. If needed, a longer settling time might have to be enforced.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Degraded pointing performance

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: enforced by do_deltaV behavior
check to ensure the referenced parameter has not been modified to violate this constraint.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: SRU Low-Radiation Calibration Frequency
flight_rule.description:
Both SRU optical heads shall be calibrated in the low-radiation regime (defined by a distance from Jupiter's center greater than 15*Rj) at least once every 365 days.
See associated flight rules: GNC-B-0029, GNC-C-0024, GNC-C-0025, GNC-B-0060, GNC-B-0042, GNC-B-0044
flight_rule.rationale: Calibrations are performed to mitigate aging and environmental effects. Aging of the sensor itself may be masked by radiation effects if there is high radiation during a calibration, and so it must be done outside. NOTE that this applies during the whole mission...the entirety of cruise is in the "low-radiation regime"
flight_rule.violation_impact: Possible, unknown degradation to science pointing

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: IMU Calibrations after Reconfiguration
flight_rule.description:
After an IMU power-cycle or gyro configuration change, the IMU must be calibrated before start of the next science observation.
See associated flight rules: GNC-B-0060, GNC-B-0039
flight_rule.rationale: The scale factor error is randomized upon power cycling the IMU (and changing IMU configuration requires power-cycling). This means that it must be calibrated before it can achieve full performance
flight_rule.violation_impact: Degraded pointing performance

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Do we need to check manually in case there's an unrequested reset or event?

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Settling Time After Engine Maneuver Completion
flight_rule.description:
The commanded maximum burn termination time of an engine maneuver must be followed by 15 minutes of quiescent time before any commanded slew.
See associated flight rules: GNC-B-0056, GNC-A-0055, GNC-B-0052, GNC-B-0050, GNC-B-0049, GNC-B-0032, GNC-B-0031
flight_rule.rationale: Quiescent time is defined as body rates in [X, Y, Z] being below [0.436, 0.175, 0.175] mrad/sec. This allows fuel slosh and dynamic modes (of the solar arrays, mag-boom, etc.) to settle so that the spacecraft can reliably follow the commanded turn. Furthermore, this time will be used to collect high rate data to produce delta-V estimates at the required precision. The adequacy of the selected 15-min settling time should be confirmed inflight. If needed, a longer settling time might have to be enforced.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Degraded pointing performance. Expend extra propellant to fight slosh during slews

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: The wait time is included in the DO_DELTA-V behavior (it is a parameter and not an argument of the behavior).

DT 09/01/21 SEQGen could monitor the "GNC_MBM_DO_DELTA_V" command execution and check the parameter value of "GNC_MBM_DV_POST_BURN_SETTLE_DELAY" is == 15.
Ensure the parameter referenced is at least 15 minutes

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Maneuver execution without valid gyro calibration
flight_rule.description:
A maneuver shall not be planned without at least one SRU Optical Head tracking unobstructed at the maneuver attitude unless the prime gyro has been calibrated within the last 27 days.
See associated flight rules: GNC-B-0026, GNC-B-0047, GNC-B-0037
flight_rule.rationale: All GNC analysis of maneuver execution performance assumes that the gyro performance would be consistent with a calibrated gyro. Before the first gyro calibration, or if the results of the last calibration are invalidated (e.g., by IMU swap, CE reset, or passage of time since the last calibration) it is necessary for GNC to be receiving the SRU data during the maneuver to ensure that GNC meets maneuver execution error requirements.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Consequence of violating the rule is a potential exceedance of GNC execution error requirements, with the associated potential downstream navigational cost for cleaning up the error. So navigation and prop cost, and perhaps failure to achieve Europa flyby target conditions.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: No Change to default3JAttitude When Not in RCSTrkSunPoint or Transitioning to 3J
flight_rule.description:
A command to change the default3JAttitude state (GNC_EXC_SET_DEFAULT_3J_ATT) shall not be issued unless GNC is in RCSTrkSunPoint.
See associated flight rule: GNC-B-0058
flight_rule.rationale: Changes to the default3JAttitude are realized only at the RCSAcquire3J to PointRCS3J transition. A command sent after this transition will be rejected by GNC, and thus, the desired attitude will not be achieved. Since the transition from RCSAcquire3J to PointRCS3J occurs autonomously (and therefore at an unknown time), commands to change the default attitude should occur only in RCSTrkSunPoint before the mode transition to RCSAcquire3J is dispatched. Note: this FR does not apply to changes to the default 3J attitude made by the motion behaviors.
flight_rule.violation_impact: The commanded is rejected and additional time and propellant is consumed to correct the spacecraft attitude once a 3J control mode is reached.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: No Change to default3JAttitude While Motion Behavior is Active
flight_rule.description:
The command to change the default3JAttitude state (GNC_EXC_SET_DEFAULT_3J_ATT) shall not be issued if a motion behavior is active.
See associated flight rule: GNC-B-0057
flight_rule.rationale: The motion behavior manager has the authority to set the state of default3JAttitude, and thus overwrite a similar ground command. If this unknowingly occurs because a motion behavior was active, then the desired attitude will not be achieved.
flight_rule.violation_impact: The command is overwritten and additional time and propellant is consumed to correct the spacecraft attitude once a 3J control mode is reached.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Secondary Pointing Constraint For Low-Altitude Flybys on RCS Control
flight_rule.description:
For all RCS controlled, low-altitude (< 10,000 km) gravity assist flybys, the spacecraft's base attitude shall be defined with an inertially fixed secondary attitude vector that yields the body-frame -Z-axis pointed at the center of the targeted flyby body while at closest approach.
See associated flight rules: GNC-A-0053, GNC-A-0057
flight_rule.rationale:
By defining the secondary pointing vector in this way, the celestial body will approximately sweep through the spacecraft YZ plane during the flyby and remain in the -Z hemisphere of the spacecraft body frame. This will (1) minimize gravity gradient torque (and thus conserve propellant) and (2) minimize SRU obstructions. The inertial vector of interest can be modeled as a SKY_RA_DEC type vector and computed in advance.
Note: current gravity assist flybys include Earth, Mars, and Ganymede.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Unexpected prop consumption and SRU obstructions.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: GNC ops procedural check

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: IMU M-matrix parameters updated and saved to NVM before JOI
flight_rule.description: No earlier than twelve days before the start of JOI, both the prime and backup IMU shall be calibrated with all four gyros on and their resulting M-matrices saved to their corresponding parameters via a GNC parameter update to both the prime and backup ECEs.
flight_rule.rationale: After an IMU calibration, the resulting M-matrix is saved only to volatile memory as the M-matrix in-use state. Upon experiencing an ECE RESET or swap, the current M-matrix in-use state will be lost, and the values set to the last stored M-matrix parameter. Note: there are different M-matrix parameters for each IMU and each gyro configuration. During JOI, both IMU-A and IMU-B will be powered on and configured to four gyros on (i.e., configuration ABCD). Thus, these exact configurations should be calibrated just before JOI and their corresponding M-matrices saved to nonvolatile memory via a GNC parameter update to both the prime and backup ECEs. "JOI" is defined as the start of the burn.
flight_rule.violation_impact: If GNC loads an outdated IMU calibration (i.e. M-matrix) due to an ECE RESET or swap during JOI, and the SRUs lose track in the high radiation environment, then GNC will not be able guarantee that the Gates pointing error requirements will be met. This exceedance will have associated delta-V and prop clean up costs.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Will be enforced by the JOI Procedure

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: SADA Hardstop Rates
flight_rule.description:
When commanding solar array articulation against the SADA hardstop, the commanded articulation rate shall not exceed 0.25 deg/sec (0.004363 rad/sec).
See associated flight rule: GNC-A-0052
flight_rule.rationale:
The SADA test program provisioned (required and tested 2x) for 10 full-speed (1.024 deg/sec) hardstop impacts and 134 slow-speed (0.25 deg/sec) impacts. The full-speed allocation is reserved for SPF use in safing responses. The slow-speed allocation is intended for ground-directed use for calibration purposes at discretion of the operations team.
Annual SADA checkout during cruise phase.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Commanding hardstop impact faster than 0.25 deg/sec may exceed the SADA qualification envelope and lead to premature wear of the SADA.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: David to discuss w/Phil Good.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Pre-burn Settle Delay for Maneuvers with RCS Slews
flight_rule.description: For maneuvers with RCS-controlled slews to/from the maneuver attitude, including JOI and JOI Demo, the duration between completing the pre-burn accelerometer calibration and the beginning of the burn shall be in the range [205, 305] seconds.
flight_rule.rationale:
This flight rule refers to the period of time in the Maneuver Behavior called the "pre-burn settle delay" combined with the wait for "T <= T(o)". The duration of time needs to be long enough to allow the RCS controller to reject attitude error that accumulated during the Control Idle period of the accelerometer calibration, but shorter than the amount of time required for the RCS controller to autonomously leave the slew controller and subsequent deadbanding errors to grow. Both the "pre-burn settle delay" (parameter: GNC_MBM_DV_PRE_BURN_SETTLE_DELAY) and burn start time, T(o) (Maneuver Behavior argument), can be adjusted in order to meet this flight rule.
Note 1: 200 seconds is the estimated maximum time to reach the DVC initial conditions (i.e., ~110sec slew when exiting Contorldle3J into PointRCS3J and ~100sec of post-slew settling). If there is a minimal slew, 300 seconds is the time at which the RCS controller switches to TRACK (deadband). Technically, could go longer than 300 s because would take some time for control errors to grow while deadbanding. Would be analysis to find breaking point. In addition, the 5 second wait time between the end of accel cal and the command to POINTRCS3J is included.
Note 2: This flight rule assumes the parameters GNC_EXC_NUM_RTI_SETTLED_SLEW_TRACK_RCS_NOMINAL_0 and GNC_EXC_NUM_RTI_SETTLED_SLEW_TRACK_RCS_NOMINAL_1 are set to 2400 and 0 respectively (i.e., 300 second settling time after a slew before the RCS controller transitions to TRACK). If either of these parameters are altered, this flight rule will need to be updated.
Note 3: Rule also applies to TCM1 from SuperSafe RCS. With known-inertia SuperSafe agilities, the post-accel-cal slew is < ~80 s. TCM1 Gates includes starting from SuperSafe TRACK deadbands, so any time after ~80 s is acceptable. But to keep the applicable to all burns, staying with [205, 305] s.
Technically, JOI and JOI Demo could be 200 s to...larger without affecting Gates significantly, but doing one flight rule to reduce analysis burden.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Larger maneuver pointing error and potentially failure to meet Gates performance requirements. Propellant cost to clean-up the navigation errors.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: GNC Ops procedural check

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Pre-burn Settle Delay for Maneuvers with RWA Slews
flight_rule.description: For maneuvers with RWA-controlled slews to/from the maneuver attitude, the duration between completing the pre-burn accelerometer calibration and the beginning of the burn shall be less than or equal to 60 seconds.
flight_rule.rationale:
This flight rule refers to the period of time in the Maneuver Behavior that includes the "pre-burn settle delay" and the wait for "T <= T(o)".The accelerometer calibration will degrade over time due to random walk which directly affects GNC's capability of meeting post-maneuver delta-V reconstruction requirements. Analysis has demonstrated that keeping this specified duration of time to under 60 seconds maintains an acceptable amount of accelerometer error while not taxing MOS too much. 60 s is not a cliff, but would require more analysis and agreement form NAV.
The "pre-burn settle delay" (parameter: GNC_MBM_DV_PRE_BURN_SETTLE_DELAY) could be set to 0 and the time of the DO_DELTAV command adjusted in order to meet this flight rule.
flight_rule.violation_impact: GNC could exceed delta-V reconstruction requirements, which could then lead to additional/more costly cleanup maneuvers, and thus greater prop consumption.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Ops process.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Primary Body Vectors for Maneuvers
flight_rule.description: When executing the DO_DELTA_V behavior, the primary body vector used to define the burn attitude shall either be GNC_VCS_MANEUVER_THRUST_AXIS_BF or GNC_VCS_POS_Z_AXIS_BF.
flight_rule.rationale: The primary body vector used to define the burn attitude is passed as an argument to the DO_DELTA_V behavior. If the angle between the intended burn direction and GNC_VCS_POS_Z_AXIS_BF exceeds the value set by the parameter GNC_DVC_COS_ZBF_DV_ALIGN_TOL, the command to execute the burn will be rejected. Note: if GNC_VCS_MANEUVER_THRUST_AXIS_BF is selected, then the angle between GNC_VCS_MANEUVER_THRUST_AXIS_BF and GNC_VCS_POS_Z_AXIS_BF must be less than the value set by the parameter GNC_DVC_COS_ZBF_DV_ALIGN_TOL to avoid violating this flight rule.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Maneuver rejected, unnecessary slews to the burn attitude potentially wasting time and prop if on RCS control

enforcement_method.enforcement_description:
Seqgen will monitor the FSW command "GNC_MBM_DO_DELTA_V" and its "burn_primary_body_vector" parameter. This parameter is based on enum "DELTAV_BURN_BODY_VEC". For this flight rule, Seqgen will check these two values of the enum: "MANEUVER_THRUST_AXIS_BF" and "DELTAV_POS_Z_AXIS_BF"

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Array delay set to zero for maneuvers with RCS slews
flight_rule.description: For maneuvers that are executed using the DeltaV motion behavior with RCS-controlled slews to/from the maneuver attitude, the Array Rotation Delay parameter shall be set to zero, so slew and solar array articulation are done in parallel.
flight_rule.rationale: If the maneuvers to-and-from the burn attitude are performed on RCS control, a non-zero Array Rotation Delay (parameter: GNC_MBM_DV_ARRAY_ROTATION_DELAY) could lead to an unpredictable slew with non-negligible delta-V. This slew would occur after the post-burn accelerometer calibration when GNC transitions from ControlIdle3J to PointRCS3J. If the delay is non-zero, this transition can trigger a slew exceeding the Gates-Pointing budget. By ensuring this delay is set to zero, the slew will be interrupted by the turn from the burn attitude.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Exceed Gates-Pointing performance requirement, thus incurring higher delta-V cleanup costs and prop consumption.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Commanding RWAs to OFF while under speed control
flight_rule.description:
Do not command RWAs to OFF if they are still under speed control. For nominal operation, powering off all RWAs should be performed in MomCntl3J mode (transitioned from either PointRCS3J or PointRWA3J), by commanding GNC_RRC_RW_GOTO_SPEEDS (0 RPM), wait for "profile_done" (or some max_dur time), followed by GNC_RRC_RW_GOTO_SPEEDS (disable all wheels), then power off RWAs GNC_RWA_POWER
Note: RWA re-configuration activity is exclude from this flight rule.
flight_rule.rationale: If the wheels were still under speed control when commanded to power off it could trigger FP, with ACS Mode going to COAST. Possible FM trip when this order is not observed. Modes this command is accepted in = MomCntl3J. Rejected in all other modes

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: RWA Prime Set
flight_rule.description:
The RWA prime set (i.e., the configuration used for control) shall be rotated such that one wheel does not spend more than 6 months as the back-up.
See associated flight rule: GNC-B-0030
flight_rule.rationale: The objective is to distribute wear on the wheels. Primarily, for evening out the radiation wear on EEE components during Tour in the Jupiter environment, and secondarily, for evening out bearing wear during Cruise and Tour.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Possible wheel degradation on those used more often

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Feed into ops procedures

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Balanced Biases
flight_rule.description:
When possible, RWA momentum biases should be done in the "balanced' configuration, using only the Y-facing engines.
See associated flight rules: GNC-A-0008, GNC-B-0038, GNC-A-0054, GNC-C-0036
flight_rule.rationale: Balanced biases minimum the deltaV imparted on the spacecraft by the event, which is important to the navigation team's orbit determination effort
flight_rule.violation_impact: Unexpected propellant cost in maneuvers to correct deltaV imparted due to biases

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: IS: Feed into ops procedures WAS: Seqgen (...information is contained as an argument to the bias behavior...)

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: SRU Photo Mode
flight_rule.description:
The SRUs should not be commanded to photo mode outside of SRU calibrations or characterizations.
See associated flight rules: GNC-B-0043, GNC-B-0044, GNC-B-0039
flight_rule.rationale: An SRU head cannot track stars while in photo mode. Therefore, if just one SRU head is powered on, then the attitude is being propagated on only IMU data when the SRU is in photo mode. An SRU calibration plan will account for this in the activity duration. Note that, if two SRUs are powered on, one may remain in track mode while the other is in photo mode.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Unintended IMU-only propagation, which could lead to excessive attitude error if the persistence is many hours

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Feed into ops procedures.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: RCS controller, X-band HGA antenna deadband selection
flight_rule.description: When operating under 3J RCS pointing control, the controller deadband should be restored to a wider (> 4 mrad) deadband setting at the conclusion of HGA telecom sessions.
flight_rule.rationale: Operating from an unnecessarily tight deadband within RCS control will consume more propellant than necessary.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Unexpected propellant usage up to the order of 10's of grams per day.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Feed into ops procedures.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: GNC parameter updates require Control Idle modes
flight_rule.description:
Before dispatching a GNC_ACS_SWAP_PARAMS command, GNC shall be commanded into a Control Idle mode (including Reset and excluding ControlIdleAcq3R).
See associated flight rules: GNC-A-0046, GNC-A-0051, GNC-A-0048, GNC-C-0026, GNC-C-0029
flight_rule.rationale: A GNC parameter update can cause the GNC algorithms to destabilize. If GNC was in a Control Active mode during any part of the algorithm destabilization period, the invalid control commands could lead to loss of control of the spacecraft. The FSW validates the GNC control mode when GNC_ACS_SWAP_PARAMS is dispatched to prevent this situation from occurring. If GNC is in a Control Active mode, the command will report failure and will not cause any parameter changes to take effect. Modes that apply are Reset, ControlIdle3R, ControlIdle3RS, ControlIdleAcq3J, ControlIdle3J, and ControlIdleCelestial. SFP parameters are not used to control the spacecraft, so they are an exception to this rule. If only SFP parameters have been updated, GNC does not need to be in Control Idle mode, and the FSW does not enforce a mode requirement.
flight_rule.violation_impact: If GNC was in a forbidden mode, the GNC_ACS_SWAP_PARAMS command would immediately report failure, and the new set of parameters would not take effect when expected. Result would be a rejected command (thanks to the FSW safeguard), and the spacecraft stability would not be affected.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Feed into ops procedure.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Control Idle State During Instrument Launch Lock and Cover Deployments
flight_rule.description:
GNC must be in ControlIdle3J for the EIS and Europa-UVS launch lock deployments and the EIS NAC and WAC, SUDA, Europa-UVS, and MASPEX instrument cover deployments. GNC shall remain in the Control Idle mode for a settling time of 1 min after each worst case deployment time.
See associated flight rules: GNC-A-0052, GNC-A-0048, GNC-C-0028, GNC-A-0046, GNC-A-0012, GNC-A-0045
flight_rule.rationale: Though expected to have much smaller dynamic impact to the Flight System than the ECM boom and REASON deployments, all instrument launch lock deployments (i.e., EIS and Europa-UVS) and cover deployments (i.e., EIS NAC and WAC, SUDA, Europa-UVS, and MASPEX) will excite dynamic signatures that are unmodeled and potentially detectable by the IMU. The effect of these signatures on GNC, including the controller response, is unverified. Since instrument deployment activities are short in duration, GNC should enter ControlIdle3J for these deployments followed by a wait time of 1 min to ensure all forces and torques exerted on the spacecraft have dissipated.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Unknown GNC response to small dynamic signatures (e.g., potential increase in pointing error and/or unnecessary fuel consumption if in RCS control).

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Feed into ops procedures.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Fix Solar Arrays for Ka-band Downlinks
flight_rule.description:
While Earth-pointed for Ka-band downlinks, the solar arrays shall not be articulated (but can remain in Sun-Tracking) from 6 min prior to the start of the downlink until its completion.
See associated flight rules: GNC-C-0023, GNC-A-0039, GNC-A-0040, GNC-A-0027, GNC-A-0016, GNC-A-0015, GNC-A-0010, GNC-C-0023
flight_rule.rationale: GNC fine pointing accuracy is only achieved when the arrays are fixed (and after the SA post-articulation settling time of 6 min). Note: if the SC remains earth-pointed continuously for several days and if the arrays are left in the Sun Tracking state during that time, then there could be rare (highly infrequent) SA deadband corrections when the array pointing error grows larger than 3 degrees. Even in these scenarios, CFDP will handle link dropouts automatically to ensure no data is lost. Since the consequences are benign, and manually stopping the arrays would increase operations complexity, the arrays may be left in Sun-Tracking mode during Ka-band downlinks. This decision was made in agreement with Mission Planning, GNC, and MOS.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Potential interrupts in Ka-band downlinks due to GNC exceeding performance threshold.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Feed into ops procedures.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: SADA (Solar Array) Agility RWA Control
flight_rule.description:
When the spacecraft is under RWA control, the maximum commanded SADA (solar array) rate and acceleration are 4.360e-3 rad/s and 1.920e-5 rad/s2, respectively.
See associated flight rules: GNC-C-0035, GNC-B-0062, GNC-B-0050, GNC-C-0034
flight_rule.rationale: These are the fastest rate and acceleration values allowable on RWA control. The controller may not be able to maintain control if faster rates are used

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: SRU photo mode buffer utilization
flight_rule.description:
Before JOI, the largest photo mode picture size allowed to be commanded is 600^2 pixels (i.e. Xpixels * Ypixels <= 600^2).
After JOI, the largest photo mode picture size allowed to be commanded 550^2 pixels (i.e. Xpixels * Ypixels <= 550^2).
flight_rule.rationale:
In high radiation, the internal SRU compression algorithm is not as efficient as when there is no radiation. Thus, the maximum amount of pixels allowed to be captured in a "photo" is 550^2.
The only GNC activity that will utilize full SRU photo buffer is "GNC_SRU_Take_Photo_Full" activity. Two sets of input arguments for controlling the photo buffer utilization to within 600^2 pixels and 550^2 pixels have been defined for Cruise and Tour phases, respectively. Merlin will load the appropriate input set according to mission phase.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Lost of SRU photo data.
