flight_rule.flight_rule_title: ECM Operational Thermal Constraints at Low Heliocentric Range
flight_rule.description: Do not power on the ECM instrument at a heliocentric range less than 0.95 AU. The MAG_POWER_ON and MAG_DO_SCIENCE behaviors both power on the instrument. If ECM was powered on by an activity that occurred at larger heliocentric range, then it should be powered off using the MAG_POWER_OFF behavior before this heliocentric range is crossed.
flight_rule.rationale: If the Sun directly heats the FG sensors at heliocentric ranges less than 0.95 AU, the sensors may rise to a temperature above the AFT limits. Given that the spacecraft spends only a short time inside of 0.95 AU, the rule should not be a significant impact to ECM operations.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Instrument health. Overheating may cause the complete loss of one or more FG sensors. There may be some spacecraft attitudes or operational time limits that would not lead to sensors overheating at low heliocentric range. However, the thermal analysis that might allow ECM to be powered on under some conditions is not mature and there are no plans to do such an analysis at this time.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description:
DT 09/27/2021 SEQGen will create an attribute to keep track of MAG powered on state and flag this FR MAG-A-0002 if this state is ON and the S/C to sun distance is less than 0.95 AU.
MAG_POWER_ON behavior is not allowed when the heliocentric range is less than 0.95 AU. MAG_DO_SCIENCE behavior is not allowed when the heliocentric range is less than 0.95 AU. If the state of the ECM power is ON, then verify that a MAG_POWER_OFF behavior is commanded before the spacecraft crosses the 0.95 AU heliocentric range inbound.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: ECM FGS non-Operational Heater Set Points for Heliocentric Range > 1.7 AU
flight_rule.description:
The ECM non operational heater low and high temperature thresholds must be set to -30.0degC and -20.0degC, respectively, when the spacecraft heliocentric range is greater than 1.7 AU. The temperature thresholds are set by issuing the command DDM_SET_SYS_PARAM_FLT (ID= xxx, vers=1, val=xxx)
The temperature thresholds are set by issuing the command DDM_SET_SYS_PARAM_FLT (ID= xxx, vers=1, val=xxx). The parameter IDs for the three nonOp FG high value thermal zones are: THRM_ECM_FG_1_ZN_CLS_NONOP_HI THRM_ECM_FG_2_ZN_CLS_NONOP_HI THRM_ECM_FG_3_ZN_CLS_NONOP_HI The parameter IDs for the three nonOp FG low value thermal zones are: THRM_ECM_FG_1_ZN_CLS_NONOP_LO THRM_ECM_FG_2_ZN_CLS_NONOP_LO THRM_ECM_FG_3_ZN_CLS_NONOP_LO Threshold values remain fixed until commanded to another value.
flight_rule.rationale: If the ECM FG non-operational heaters are not enabled for heliocentric ranges greater than 1.7 > AU when the instrument is off, thermal modeling indicates that the ECM FG sensors may exceed their cold Non-OP AFT limits. Modeling also indicates that if the heaters were to become stuck in the ON position, that the heater boards would not overheat beyond this distance. After this heliocentric range, solar flux reduces to a range that temperature difference between heater board and the sensor head increases. This means higher temperature setpoint is required to keep the sensor head above -120C.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Instrument Health. Cooling any of the three FG sensors below their AFT limits may result in permanent damage to the FG sensor.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: ECM FGS Operational Heater Control at Heliocentric Range < 2.5 AU
flight_rule.description: Do not enable the ECM internal FG operational heater controls for longer than 1 minute when the heliocentric range is less than 2.5 AU.
flight_rule.rationale:
If the ECM FG operational heaters were to fail with the heaters in the ON condition, the resistors on the FGS Heater Board may be heated beyond the Qual limits. Instrument fault protection is designed to shut the instrument down before the heater board operational resistors over heat. If the operational heaters are not enabled, they can't fail in the ON state. This rule serves two purposes. First it prevents a fault protection response (power OFF) in the event of a heater anomaly (failed ON) during a critical calibration event. Secondly it protects the instrument against the very unlikely two-fault scenario where faults occur in the heater (failed ON) and the ECM fault management system (did not request power OFF when temperature exceeded threshold). When the operational heater is enabled during the post deployment checkout in order to verify that the operational heaters are functional, they must be disabled within one minute. Additionally, the instrument should be powered off shortly (30 seconds) thereafter to ensure that power is not available to these heaters.
Background: The only way to command the ECM operation heater control state is by sending a command file using the MAG_SEND_CMD_FILE (fileToLoad) command.
The parameter for this command is the name of the ECM configuration file to be loaded.
ECM configuration file names specify whether or not the operational heater controls are enabled or disabled ("OpsHtrsOn", "OpsHtrsOff").
flight_rule.violation_impact: Instrument Health - If the operational heaters were to fail with the heaters in the ON condition, and the ECM fault response management system (FRMS) was not enabled or did not respond properly, then the FG sensors might be permanently damaged by over-heating. The more likely result of an operation FG heater failing in the ON state would be that the FRMS system would power off ECM. However, not enabling the FG ops heaters provides an addition level of protection for the instrument and the data return. ECM is only used at low heliocentric range for critical calibration and characterization activities.

reference_info.reference_document: JPL D-103370 Europa Clipper Magnetometer (ECM) FPGA Specification
D-103374 Europa Clipper Magnetometer (ECM) Command & Telemetry Dictionary

enforcement_method.enforcement_description:
Instrument team check of controlling table/file load
Verify that the command file name contains "OpsHtrsOff" when the instrument is powered on a low heliocentric range.
Also verify that any register_write or block_register_write commands in the file that modify registers 0x03, 0x0B, or 0x13
sets bit 1 of register 0x03 to 0 (FG1 htr disable) sets bit 1 of register 0x0B to 0 (FG2 htr disable) sets bit 1 of register 0x13 to 0 (FG3 htr disable)
The only time during the mission when the operational heaters should be enabled when the heliocentric range is less than 2.5 AU is during the post-launch instrument checkout following the boom deployment. If there is any issue, ECM Ops needs to know as soon as possible. This allows the team time to perform additional tests if necessary and develop operational work-arounds in the event of an instrument component failure. During the check-out, the ECM team would like to verify that the heaters and related circuits survived the launch. During this special time period, ECM can be configured to enable the operational heaters for no longer than about 1 minute. This is enough time to see a change in the power draw and temperature in the instrument housekeeping data which is generated every 10 seconds when the instrument is in the high-rate mode. The heaters are switched on and then off again by loading instrument configuration files. The instrument team will verify by visual inspection that the post launch checkout sequence contains commands to send a configuration file that enables the heaters in high-rate mode, and then sends another configuration file that disables the operational heaters in high-rate mode no more than 60 seconds or less than 50 seconds after sending the first file. These will be the last activities in the ECM check out sequence before the instrument is powered off for the final time in the sequence a minute later. There is nothing magical about the choice of one minute for the maximum duration. In one minute, ECM should receive 4-6 HSK packets that confirm that the heaters are operational. If the actual duration is slightly longer (00:01:05) due to command execution latency it won't be a problem. ECM sequence verification will check the file load command separation with the understanding that the command execution separation times could be a few seconds longer.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: ECM FGS Operational Heater Control at Heliocentric Range > 2.5 AU
flight_rule.description: The commands to enable ECM internal FG operational heater controls must be sequenced or issued from FSW behaviors no sooner than 3 seconds nor later than 13 seconds following a MAG_POWER_ON behavior when the heliocentric range is greater than 2.5 AU.
flight_rule.rationale:
If ECM sensors are operated without operational heater control at heliocentric ranges greater than 2.5 AU, the sensors may exceed their lower AFT limits.
The MAG_POWER_ON behavior does not enable the ECM fault management system nor does it enable the FG operational heaters. These actions must be performed by sending an appropriate command file by using the MAG_SEND_CMD_FILE(fileToLoad) command. The ECM configuration files (e.g. ECM_Configure*_OpsHtrsOff) include the operational heater configuration in the file name by convention. A file with the name ECM_Configure*_OpsHtrsOn must be loaded on the spacecraft before it reaches a heliocentric range of 2.5 AU and this file must be used as the parameter for the MAG_SEND_CMD_FILE command.
The MAG_DO_SCIENCE(fileToLoad) behavior powers on the instrument and issues the MAG_SEND_CMD_FILE(fileToLoad) command as soon as the instrument power on is complete (3 seconds). The parameter filename should indicate that the configuration file has been built to enable the operational heaters. This file must be loaded on the spacecraft before it is used by the MAG_DO_SCIENCE behavior regardless of heliocentric range.
It is understood that is a latency between the time that a command is issued by either sequence or behavior and when that command is executed. This rule is intended to minimize the total time to command execution by requiring that the commands be issued very shortly after the instrument is powered on.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Instrument Health - The FG sensors may be permanently damaged if their temperature falls below the lower AFT thermal limit.

Verify that any register_write or block_register_write commands in the file that modify registers 0x03, 0x0B, or 0x13

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: MAGboom deployment
flight_rule.description:
The MAGboom must be deployed at a heliocentric range less than 1.07 AU.
See related flight rule: MAG-A-0010
flight_rule.rationale: Before the boom can be deployed the boom canister must be heated to more than 20 deg C for at least 4 hours to reduce the stiffness of the ECM cable harness and cable drag during deployment. After a heliocentric range of 1.07 AU, there is insufficient solar illumination on the arrays to guarantee the availability of the power required to heat the canister prior to boom deployment.
flight_rule.violation_impact: The MAG boom cannot be deployed if the available power too low to properly heat the boom canister prior to deployment. Attempting to power the mag boom canister heaters with a bus voltage less than 27.8 may cause an under voltage safing of the spacecraft. Attempting to deploy the boom when the harness has not been heated as planned may result in a failed or partial boom deployment. Delayed deployment would result in lost observations that would be used for future observation design. There is also a concern that if the sensor harness becomes very cold for an extended period of time that it may not perform as expected at the next opportunity near the Earth flyby. A successful ECM experiment requires that the boom is deployed and the preferred time is within the first 30 days after launch when the heliocentric range is also less than 1.07 AU.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: ECM In-Flight Operational Thermal Constraints at Low Earth Altitude
flight_rule.description: The ECM FG sensors must be powered off in-flight at Earth altitudes less than 3000 km.
flight_rule.rationale: Thermal modeling indicates that the FG sensors may exceed the hot AFTs because of the effects of the Earth's albedo and IR at altitudes less than 3000 km during the Earth flyby. Powering off the FG sensors (MAG_SHUTDOWN) removes the Ohmic heating that having them powered on would add to the system. FG sensors can be powered on again (MAG_MEASURE) once the spacecraft altitude is above 3000 km.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Instrument Health - Even with the operational heaters off, thermal modeling indicates that the ECM FG sensors may exceed their AFTs at Earth altitudes less than 3000 km. Damage to the FG sensors could be permanent.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description:
In the Earth flyby sequence, verify that MAG_SHUTDOWN is commanded before the predicted spacecraft altitude is less than 3000 km.
In the Earth flyby sequence, verify that MAG_MEASURE is not commanded while the predicted spacecraft altitude is less than 3000 km.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: ECM Power On Thermal Stabilization Time
flight_rule.description: ECM should be powered on for at least 30 minutes before acquiring L1 science or calibration data in order for the electronics and sensors to thermally stabilize.
flight_rule.rationale:
ECM calibration is a function of both sensor and electronics temperature and the data quality is expected to be degraded during the thermal stabilization time.
This includes both the warm-up time for the electronics, and the time to stabilize after the sensors swap over from spacecraft (non-Op) to instrument (Op) thermal control.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Reduced data quality resulting from an unstable thermal environment.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Verify that at least 30 minutes have elapsed since a MAG_POWER_ON or MAG_DO_SCIENCE command before the start of any satellite flyby activity, ECM calibration activity, or EMI/EMC test activity. ECM_MagBackgroundCal (offset) activities are exempt from this restriction. For these long duration activities, the initial 30 minutes of data can be excluded from analysis on the ground.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: MAG_NO_OP Command Following a ECE side swap
flight_rule.description: Following an Avionics ECE side swap, a MAG_NO_OP command must be issued in order to reestablish communication with Avionics if ECM is powered on when the swap occurs. This command should be issued at the first possible opportunity if ECM is still powered on.
flight_rule.rationale: Following an Avionics ECE side swap, an MAG_NO_OP command must be issued prior to any other commanding in order to reestablish communication with Avionics if ECM is powered on when the swap occurs. The MAG power on behaviors issue a MAG_NO_OP command so this is only necessary if the swap occurs while ECM is powered on.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Loss of an instrument command. The first command following a ECE side swap will re-establish communication with Avionics but it will not be acted on by ECM.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Verify that a MAG_NO_OP command is issued before any other MAG commands following a CEU side swap that occurred when ECM was powered on.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Don't command ECM block_register_write while the ECM FRMS is enabled.
flight_rule.description: Do not issue an ECM block_register_write command while the internal ECM Fault Response Management System (FRMS) is enabled. The persistence values stored in registers 64-71 (0x40 - 0x47) must all be set to their default values of 0x0000 prior writing to any registers in order to disable the FRMS. Fault protection must be enabled again after all other register values have been set by setting the persistence values to their nominal values.
flight_rule.rationale: Changing register values with fault protection enabled may trigger an unintended fault response that could result in the loss of science and/or health and safety data due to invalid data in the FPGA registers.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Potential loss of science and/or health and safety data.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: The ECM Ops team shall verify that that any changes to the FPGA configuration that occur after the FRMS has been enabled, disable the FRMS before writing to any other portion of the FPGA register space. This requires that the first block register write command (OpCode 0xC800) be one that sets the values of registers 64-71 (0x40 - 0x47) to their default values of 0x0000. The last write command in the command file shall be a block register write that sets these registers back to their nominal values to re-enable the FRMS.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Follow proper fg_sync bit usage
flight_rule.description: A pair of single register write commands must be issued to assert (1) and release (0) the fg_sync bit in register 0x50 whenever any of the FG registers (range 0x00 - 0x1F) is modified. Asserting the fg_sync bit clears the data processing chain. Releasing the fg_sync bit resumes FG data processing.
flight_rule.rationale: Any change to the FG parameters invalidates the existing data processing chain. Asserting the fg_sync bit clears the chain so that a clean data processing chain can be established once new parameters are in place. Releasing the fg_sync bit resumes normal data processing using the new parameters.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Potential loss of science and/or health and safety data.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: The ECM Ops Team shall verify that the fg_sync bit (register 0x50, bit 10) is asserted (set to 1) before any changes are made to the FG register space (range 0x00 - 0x1F) and then released (set to 0) before operations resume. Although these bits can be set as part of a block write operation, best practice is to use a single register write command with RegAdr[7:0] = 0x50, Mask[15:0] = 0xFBFF,RegData[15:0]=0x0001 to assert the fg_sync bit and RegAdr[7:0] = 0x50, Mask[15:0] = 0xFBFF,RegData[15:0]=0x0000 to release it.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Do not command the ECM into a ground-only test mode in flight.
flight_rule.description: Don't command ECM into the ground test mode (0x7) during flight
flight_rule.rationale:
If the ground-only test mode is commanded in flight, the science data will likely be corrupted and the source of the corruption may be difficult to locate. The resulting data will not appear to be a normal test pattern, as would occur on the ground.
The ECM has eight possible modes, science [0x0] and seven test modes (register 0x50, bits 4:2]. Of the test modes, one is designed for ground testing only (0x7).
flight_rule.violation_impact: Loss of science data

enforcement_method.enforcement_description:
If necessary, test modes will be commanded by loading a special configuration file load that will write non-standard values to addresses FPGA 0x50 and 0x51.
FG output data modes are set in register 0x50, bits [4:2]. The nominal value for science mode is 0x00. The ground-only text mode has the value 0x7. The ECM Ops engineer shall verify that these bits are never set to 0x7 in-flight.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Always do a full register read immediately after any command file register writes
flight_rule.description: ECM Ops shall always command a complete readout of the ECM registers (requires 3 block register read commands) immediately following any instrument commanding that directly uses the register write or block register write commands in a command file. Low level commanding of this type is done by using the FSW MAG_SEND_CMD_FILE command. The register read commands should be included in the same command file that issues the register write commands.
flight_rule.rationale: Small errors or unwanted values in the FPGA register space may result in off-nominal instrument performance. If these differences are small, they may be very difficult to diagnose. Having a full register readout allows the operations team to verify that the changes than have been made to the instrument are exactly the intended changes.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Small errors or unwanted values in the FPGA register space may result in off-nominal instrument performance.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: The ECM Ops team shall verify that the last 3 commands in any command file sent to the instrument are block register reads (OpCode 0xC900) that read out the entire FPGA register states: RegAdrStart=0x000,RegAdrEnd=0x001F RegAdrStart=0x020,RegAdrEnd=0x003F RegAdrStart=0x040,RegAdrEnd=0x0057

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: MAG_SET_AID_BIN commanding at the start of new activities when ECM is powered ON.
flight_rule.description: All ECM activities that begin with ECM previously powered on must issue a MAG_SET_AID_BIN command within the first 9 seconds of the new activity start time. ECM inserts the most recently received AID and BIN values into the science data packet value headers. Receipt of new AID and BIN values results in the instrument sending two meta-data packets, the first closes the previous AID and the second opens an new one. The BIN value is used by the FSW for downlink prioritization and the AID value is used by the GDS system for data accountability.
flight_rule.rationale: Since every MAG packet is required to have a unique AID value, the value must be assigned before any data are written. Assigning the value within the first 9 seconds of any activity guarantees that every packet has an AID value since that fastest data packet creation rate is every 10 seconds, and the value is assigned when the packet is complete. Assigning an AID does not itself assure that the AID value is unique.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Loss of data accountability. MAG packets assigned to incorrect or default AID values and/or downlink priority bins.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Procedural, manual

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: MAG_SET_AID_BIN commanding after commanding an ECM power on
flight_rule.description: A MAG_SET_AID_BIN command should be issued no more than 15 seconds after a sequenced ECM power on event (MAG_POWER_ON, MAG_DO_SCIENCE) in order load a unique data accountability identifier into the instrument.
flight_rule.rationale:
ECM does not have a memory keep alive function that would allow it to retain the last known values of AID and BIN. At power on, both of these values default to zero. In order to uniquely identify the ECM data for accountability purposes, and set the appropriate downlink priority bin, a MAG_SET_AID_BIN must be issued. It takes 3 seconds for ECM to fully power on, and another 10 seconds for a standard configuration file to clock out. If the MAG_SET_AID_BIN command is sent during the ECM configuration, the command will not be executed until the configuration is complete, rather than being rejected. Best practice would be to sequence the MAG_SET_AID_BIN command 15 seconds after the MAG_DO_SCIENCE or MAG_POWER_ON behavior commands so that exact timing of the action is known.
Spacecraft flight software may issue a MAG_DO_SCIENCE command in response in response to ECM FRMS requests to power cycle and resume operations. If this occurs, all ECM data packets will be marked with the default values AID and BIN until a command can be sent to change them.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Loss of data accountability. MAG packets assigned to default AID values and downlink priority bins.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Manual, procedural

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Command file loaded to spacecraft before being used.
flight_rule.description: Any command file that is a parameter in a MAG_SEND_CMD_FILE or MAG_DO_SCIENCE command must be loaded on the spacecraft before it can be referenced.
flight_rule.rationale: ECM is configured for operations by sending command files, either by using the MAG_SEND_CMD_FILE or MAG_DO_SCIENCE commands. The command file name that is the parameter of these commands must be loaded to the spacecraft or the commands will fail. The MAG_DO_SCIENCE behavior aborts if the fileload fails, leaving ECM powered on but not configured.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Verification that a referenced command file has been previously loaded to the S/C is part of the MAG team sequence review procedure. However, if the ECM operator fails to catch such an error the instrument will not be correctly configured. When the first FG temperature falls to the low temperature AFT limit, FSW will power down ECM to prevent permanent damage.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Verify that any command file that is referenced by a MAG_SEND_CMD_FILE or MAG_DO_SCIENCE has been previously uploaded to the spacecraft.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: MASPEX Maintenance - Cryocooler
flight_rule.description: The MASPEX Cryocooler shall be operated for not less than 30 minutes, at least once every 90 days.
flight_rule.rationale: If the cryocooler is not exercised periodically, there is a risk that the moving parts might seize up.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Hardware damage; possible complete loss of cryocooler functionality. Loss of trace species and isotopic science enabled by cryocooler.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Timing of MASPEX vacuum cover release
flight_rule.description:
The deployment of the MASPEX vacuum cover shall occur at least 3 weeks after the last planned maneuver > 20m/s, and before the first targeted flyby subsequent to JOI.
See associated flight rules: MASP-A-0003
flight_rule.rationale:
The vacuum cover deployment is an irreversible, one time process which unseals the instrument. This should not be executed until after the spacecraft has completed its major burns to ensure engine material from the major burns does not contaminate the instrument.
The vacuum cover deployment is a two step Arm and Fire process. Both Arm and Fire steps are restricted by this flight rule to safeguard against early actuation.
The spacecraft commands that control this deployment: MASP_GIS_ARM_COVER_HOP MASP_GIS_FIRE_COVER_HOP
flight_rule.violation_impact:
Decreased sensitivity due to contamination.
If the vacuum cover deployment command is executed prematurely, the instrument would be contaminated during the spacecraft burns which would significantly degrade science capabilities until after a decontamination activity can be performed.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description:
Manual check of instrument command file for the following commands: MASP_GIS_ARM_COVER_HOP MASP_GIS_FIRE_COVER_HOP
Ensure that they are not included in uplink products.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Radiative Heat Flux
flight_rule.description: The MISE radiator shall not be subjected to a greater than 3 hour moving time average net incident radiative heat flux > 32 W/m^2 between 34 hours and 11.5 hours prior to all MISE science and calibration activities.
flight_rule.rationale: This must be met in order for the MISE Instrument to maintain all subassembly temperatures to within the AFTs defined in the TRT.
flight_rule.violation_impact: If the MISE subassemblies are hotter than AFT temperatures defined in the TRT during calibration or science data take, SNR cannot be met, impacting science objectives and jeopardizing level-1 science goals.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description:
Sloan provided an algorithm, that was provided by MISE, that can be modeled in Merlin and used for the check the rule.
The algorithm in question is:
Flux on radiator: 56.9*(4.9/d_sun)^2*cos(theta_sun) + 2 W/m^2
where d_sun is spacecraft Sun range in AU theta_sun is the angle between the MISE radiator boresight and the sun. Note solar flux is scaled based on flux at 4.9 AU. The 2W at the end is the IR contribution from NAC and the reflected solar.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Never Close Launch Locks in Flight
flight_rule.description: After launch, the CEU launch locks must never be commanded closed (engaged).
flight_rule.rationale: Doing so risks subsequent damage to the CEU by commanding cryocooler operation.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Damaging the CEU will prevent proper operation of the MISE cryocooler which could prevent proper cooling of the MISE instrument and a reduction in SNR.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Manual check by instrument.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Scan mirror position during S/C propulsion and thruster activities
flight_rule.description: The MISE Scan Mirror shall be in its closed position during any S/C propulsion and thruster activities.
flight_rule.rationale: This is to ensure particulate does not enter the instrument through entrance baffle contaminating the optical surfaces.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Contamination of optical surfaces can lead to permanent degradation of optical performance and in turn impact SNR, jeopardizing level-1 science objectives.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: MISE internal commanding -- instrument team check (with input on planned maneuvers and other thruster activities)

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Do not set Cryocooler Peak Drive voltage above 18 V
flight_rule.description: Do not apply more than 18 V as the Peak Drive Voltage for the cryocooler.
flight_rule.rationale:
So as to not exceed 30 W output from the CEU to the cryocooler, do not apply more than 18 V as the Peak Drive Voltage for the CEU. The CEU capability is limited by the worst case analysis, but is not constrained by the 30 W within CEU registers.
18V limit ensures 1.8 A avg limit on common mode choke.
Set the following command: MISE_MEM_STR_LOAD(1, 2, 6, 1340)
flight_rule.violation_impact: Violates JPL current de-rating, represents risk to hardware.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: This will enforced via MISE-Simplex

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Set the MISE Autonomy Bit 2 = 1 (On) prior to powering on the MISE cryocooler to COOL or VOLT_TEST mode.
flight_rule.description: Set the MISE Autonomy Bit 2 = 1 (On) prior to powering on the MISE cryocooler to COOL or VOLT_TEST mode. This sets the MISE_CCA_WARMUP_ZN fault protection limits from the min Non-Op AFT (135 K) to the min Op AFT (195K).
flight_rule.rationale:
The cryocooler compressor has hard stops for the pistons. If this power is exceed, the pistons will hit the hard stops. This is mitigated by using the cyrocooler warmup and operational heater.
Do not drive the cooler with more than 15 Vrms (~40 W) at 135 Hz when turning it on with the expander temperature at or below 195 K.
If T < 195 K on the DPU cryocooler temperature sensor (status packet IFC 0/5), exceeding 22 W input power to the cryocooler could result in hardware damage.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Hitting of hard stops could damage hardware or degrade the performance of the cryocooler.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Enforced via MISE-Simplex

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Do not command cryocooler motor voltage > 1.5 V while CEU Launch Locks are engaged.
flight_rule.description: Do not command cryocooler motor voltage more than 1.5 V while the CEU launch locks are engaged (relays closed) or before the relays are verified open in flight. Set parameter: MISE_MEM_STR_LOAD_(1, 2, 10, 372)
flight_rule.rationale: Commanding voltages higher than this could damage the CEU if locks are engaged.
flight_rule.violation_impact: High voltages may damage the CEU.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: via SIMPLEX

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Open Launch Locks before Cryocooler First Operation in Flight
flight_rule.description: The CEU launch locks must be disengaged (relays open, unlocked) before the first powered cryocooler operation in flight. Send the MISE_COOL_OP(Unlock) command.
flight_rule.rationale:
After launch and during the first MISE checkout, the command MISE_COOL_OP(launch unlock) must be sent before any other MISE_COOL_OP command.
Disengagement (relays opened, unlocked) must be verified before supplying operational power to the cryocooler. This verification activity will involve applying low level voltages (1.5 V) through the H-bridge to verify relay state and apply power to the cryocooler. This activity involves use of the MISE_COOL_OP(voltage test) command.
Note that the MISE_COOL_OP(temp) command behavior includes a CEU command to disengage the launch locks. The MISE_COOL_OP(voltage test) command behavior does NOT include a CEU command to disengage the launch locks.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Commanding cryocooler operation with launch locks engaged will likely damage the CEU.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: via SIMPLEX.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Do not use MISE_MAC_SAVE, MISE_MAC_RESTORE, or MISE_MAC_READ while running MISE_MAC_DEF.
flight_rule.description: MISE_MAC_SAVE and MISE_MAC_RESTORE must not be used while a macro is being compiled. Similarly, macro dumps via MISE_MAC_READ and macro define cannot occur at the same time.

flight_rule.violation_impact: Macro state could become corrupted, resulting in unexpected instrument behavior.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Only operate cryocooler at a drive frequency of 135 Hz
flight_rule.description:
Only operate cryocooler at a drive frequency of 135 Hz.
Set MISE_MEM_STR_LOAD(1, 0, 16, 11574)
flight_rule.rationale: Rationale is that the cooler pistons may hit hard stops at the AFT cold at lower drive frequencies. MISE can operate at lower drive frequencies, but at higher cryocooler temperatures.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Hitting of hard stops could damage hardware or degrade the performance of the cryocooler.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Open CEU launch locks prior to operating cryocooler in voltage test mode
flight_rule.description: Always issue the MISE_COOL_OP(Unlock) command before issuing the MISE_COOL_OP(Voltage Test) command.
flight_rule.rationale: MISE_COOL_OP(VoltTest) command does not include the behavior to open launch locks to ensure a safe operating condition.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Potential damage to the CEU if voltage test mode is run at high voltage with launch lock relays closed.

flight_rule.rationale: The decontamination heaters will prevent MISE from being able to reach or maintain operational temperatures. The decontamination heaters may also increase EMI noise on the detector.

This impact can be to pointing or to noise if in the FPA. Increased noise in frame data will reduce SNR for MISE potentially not meeting mission science objectives.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: FPIE/FPA Register Setting before Frame Data Acquisition
flight_rule.description: Prior to each instance of frame acquisition, using MISE_FRAME_CAPTURE or MISE_FRAME_READ commands, the FPIE and FPA registers shall be configured using MISE instrument commands.

flight_rule.description: Prior to each instance of frame acquisition using MISE_FRAME_CAPTURE or MISE_FRAME_READ commands, the cryocooler control heater mode shall be either ON or OFF (i.e. not under DPU FSW control)
flight_rule.rationale: This is to reduce the risk of EMI noise in frame data.

flight_rule.description: MISE shall not transfer data to the spacecraft during a BDS filter, cross-string copy or radiation maintenance activity.

flight_rule.description: Do not define macros (MISE_MAC_DEF/MISE_MAC_ENDDEF) while macros are executing.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Limit macro stack depth to <=32
flight_rule.description: The number of MISE_MAC_NEST and MISE_MAC_LOOP_BEG/END commands contained within a macro and all its called macros shall not violate the following equation: 2*MAC_NEST_calls + 3*MAC_LOOP_calls <= 32
flight_rule.rationale: Do not nest too deeply. One macro can call another or can execute loops. Both macro calls and loops can be nested. Loop nesting depth is traded with macro nesting depth. Each running macro context has a 32-element stack. Each macro call uses two elements; each loop uses three elements. All MISE_MAC_NEST and MISE_MAC_LOOP_BEG/END calls from all macros nested within a defined macro must be taken into account. Once all nested and looped macros are expanded, the number of MAC_MAC_NEST and MISE_MAC_LOOP_BEG/END must satisfy the following equation: 2*MAC_NEST_calls + 3*MAC_LOOP_calls <= 32. MISE_MAC_RUN commands operates on its own "thread," starting another 32-element stack.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Filling up a macro's element stack will result in a commanding error, leaving the instrument in an uncertain state, resulting in data loss.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: via SIMPLEX

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: MISE_MAC_LOOP_BEG shall be paired with a MISE_MAC_LOOP_END
flight_rule.description: MISE_MAC_LOOP_BEG and MISE_MAC_LOOP_END must be paired correctly. Each MISE_MAC_LOOP_BEG must be followed by a MISE_MAC_LOOP_END.
flight_rule.rationale: When unpaired, the loop is not properly defined. For instance, without MISE_MAC_LOOP_END, the loop index is never decrimented.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Could command unwanted commands or states, harming science.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: via SIMPLEX

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Macro loops shall contain a MISE_MAC_DELAY command
flight_rule.description: Avoid macro loops without MISE_MAC_DELAY occurring in the loop. The minimum delay time in a loop is 1 seconds.
flight_rule.rationale:
This could shut out low priority processes and cause a watchdog reset.
Putting it anywhere within the loop is acceptable.
flight_rule.violation_impact: This could shut out low priority processes and cause a watchdog reset, resulting in instrument going to boot mode and loss of science.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: via SIMPLEX

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Do not run more than 64 macros at the same time
flight_rule.description: Do not run more than 64 macros at the same time.
flight_rule.rationale: Up to 64 macros can be running concurrently. Macros are started by the user via MISE_MAC_RUN(). If this command would result in more than 64 macros running, the command would be rejected. There is also internal software mechanism for starting macros. Examples are in the autonomy system and observation control. If these would result in more than 64 macros running, an alarm is generated. A timeline and observation(s) could be constructed to trigger this alarm.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Failure to run desired macro, which could result in loss of science.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: via SIMPLEX

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Cube numbers should be set deterministically with the MISE_NVSTORE_CUBE_SET command
flight_rule.description:
Cube numbers should be set deterministically with the MISE_NVSTORE_CUBE_SET command.
Do not use MISE_NVSTORE_CUBE.
flight_rule.rationale: Data should be traced to known cube numbers. Setting cube numbers in ways other than this may make it more difficult to link a specific cube number with a given dataset
flight_rule.violation_impact: Data could be stored in an unanticipated cube, and so might not be transfered to the spacecraft as intented. Also, different datasets could then be merged together, creating confusion in analysis.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: via SIMPLEX

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Scanner stall detection limits
flight_rule.description: MISE scanner stall error threshold parameter shall be set to 1.500 deg / 34953 counts. MISE stall error count threshold shall be set to 999 counts.
flight_rule.rationale:
These stall detection parameter limits have been tested in with the MISE FM in the I&T campaign and have reliably detected scanner stalls without generating false positives.
MISE_MEM_STR_LOAD, 1, 4, 86, 0, 0, 136, 137 # Set Stall Error Thresh to 1.500 deg. Equivalent 4-byte int is 34953.
MISE_MEM_STR_LOAD, 1, 2, 90, 3, 231 # Set Stall Error Count Thresh to 999 counts/s. Equivalent 2-byte short is 999.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Using different scanner stall detection parameters may lead to false positive stall detections, or undetected scanner stalls, either of which may result in unnecessary loss of science observations.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: via SIMPLEX

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Synchronize frame acquisition start with scanner profile motion
flight_rule.description: The MISE_OBS_TIMELINE profile delay shall match the relative start time of frame acquisition.
flight_rule.rationale: MISE_OBS_TIMELINE delay arguments for start of scanner profile motion shall be synchronized with the cumulative MISE_OBS_SEQUENCE delay arguments to the start of macro where frame acquisition occurs. This ensures that frame acquisition timing is aligned with scanner motion.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Loss of science data, Scanner may not be pointed at the expected location if this rule is violated.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: DPU and CEU Power Order
flight_rule.description: Always power on the DPU before the CEU.
flight_rule.rationale: The DPU provides the sole communication path from the CEU. If the CEU is powered on without the DPU powered on, then the CEU state is not reported to the ground team.
flight_rule.violation_impact: There is no hardware risk associated with powering the CEU on first.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Do not command the cryocooler warm-up heater off. Set cryocooler warm-up heater to non-op setpoints when not in use.
flight_rule.description:
Do not command the cryocooler warm-up heater off. Instead, command the spacecraft to change between operational and non-operational setpoints. The warm-up heater serves as a backup heater for a failed survival heater.
Do not command the cryocooler warm-up heater off. Set cryocooler warm-up heater to non-op setpoints when not in use.
flight_rule.rationale: Mitigation for a potential MISE cryocooler survival heater failure on anomaly.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: PIMS in Survival Mode during engine use
flight_rule.description: PIMS Upper and PIMS Lower have to be in Survival Mode 10 minutes before any planned engine firing, during the firing, and for at least 10 minutes afterwards.
flight_rule.rationale: Due to the proximity of PIMS Lower to the engines, whenever any material exits the engine nozzle there could be enough ambient pressure for high voltage surfaces of PIMS to short to grounded surfaces through an arc. Survival mode means that PIMS is powered Off and the spacecraft survival heaters are keeping PIMS within non-op AFTs. The 10 minute period was selected to be overly conservative and is not based on any analysis.
flight_rule.violation_impact: PIMS may experience a high voltage arc, which could damage PIMS or the rest of the FS.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: PIMS Not Powered at Sun Range <0.98AU
flight_rule.description: The PIMS instruments (Upper and Lower) shall be in Survival mode at sun ranges <0.98 AU.
flight_rule.rationale: The PIMS instrument CDR thermal analysis shows that the PIMS electronics bank will exceed operating temp at 1 AU after 1 hour. Survival mode means that PIMS is powered Off and the spacecraft survival heaters are keeping PIMS within non-op AFTs.
flight_rule.violation_impact: PIMS could violate the Launch and Cruise operating AFT.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Engine Through-Put Consumable Management
flight_rule.description:
The through-put of each engine shall not exceed 605 kg (1,333 lbm).
See associated flight rules: PROP-A-0016, PROP-A-0015
flight_rule.rationale:
The purpose of this flight rule is to mandate the use of the engines evenly under the qualified limits for through-put. This will require operations to trend the through-put, and have predictions for usage throughout the mission. This information will allow the operators to make a decision about when they need to rotate the in-use engines for maneuvers to ensure that the consumable is not exceeded. Expectation is that the z-pointed engine will be of most concern; y-pointed engine usage is not anticipated to exceed this threshold.
Note: it is preferred to vary the initial engine usage over the course of the mission, to distribute the consumable usage and to provide robustness to engine swaps.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Possible engine failure

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Iron Nitrate Flushing
flight_rule.description:
The propulsion subsystems iron nitrate flushings shall take place according the following schedule:
First Flush - Flush at 80 +/- 20 days after propellant priming; all 12 engines per string shall be fired for at least 1.5 seconds.
Second Flush - Flush at 220 +/- 30 days after first flush; all 12 engines per string shall be fired for at least 1.5 seconds.
Third Flush - IF JOI has not been reached, flush at 1,000 +/- 30 days after second flush, all 12 engines per string shall be fired for at least 1.5 seconds. - IF JOI has been reached AND B-side has NOT been utilized since JOI, or has had a cumulative engine on-time less than 18 seconds (from any combination or single engine) , flush at 1,000 +/- 30 days after second flush. - Only the unused engines on the A-side engine banks shall be fired for 2 seconds. - All 12 B-side engines shall be fired for at least 1.5 seconds. - OTHERWISE, flush at 1,000 +/- 30 days after second flush, only the unused engines shall be fired for 2 seconds with annual A-side and B-side swaps.
Post JOI, assuming annual engine bank swaps is implemented, only the non-used engines will need to be flushed every 730+/- 30 days. The burn time for these engines shall be 2 seconds.
flight_rule.rationale: Iron nitrate formation can cause issues for the bipropellant propulsion system.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Degraded performance or even propulsion subsystem failure

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Prop Ops team to check manually

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Backup PCV opening before maneuvers

flight_rule.violation_impact: High-pressure latch valve (APC latch valve) loss of seal, resulting in single seat between pressurant tanks and propellant tanks.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Tank Pressure Differential limits

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Voltage Trip Load
flight_rule.description:
The total spacecraft load shall not exceed the safe operating area equations defined in JPL IOM 3462_20_010, Safe Operating Area (SOA) in Figure 3 "LOE and UV SOA" region. The SOA defines the maximum 2 minute current below which a fault response is avoided.
During nominal ops: MaxPulseCurrent <= 196.67x -42.17 and MaxPulseCurrent <= 66A During low energy fault ops: MaxPulseCurrent <= 196.67x + 7 and MaxPulseCurrent <= 66A Where x = battery SOC under load
See associated flight rules: PWR-A-0003, PWR-A-0012, PWR-A-0010
flight_rule.rationale:
Discharge current exceeds battery SOC / current profile for more than 2 minutes presented in the figure will result in a Fault Protection low energy undervoltage response.
See reference info for relevant ECRs
flight_rule.violation_impact:
During nominal ops, if the MaxPulseCurrent violates the "nominal ops" constraint noted in the FR Description for 2 minutes or longer, then Fault Protection will initiate a Low Energy response.
When Fault Protection has initiated the low energy response, the system is in Low Energy Fault ops. During Low Energy Fault ops, if the MaxPulseCurrent violates the "low energy fault ops" constraint noted in the FR Description for 2 minutes or longer, then the power hardware will initiate a load shed, turning off all loads NOT on critical switches.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Enforce Wing Current Limit
flight_rule.description:
The wing current limiter shall be set to 10A or 12A when spacecraft sun distance is <= 4.9 AU.
See associated flight rules: PWR-C-0005, PWR-B-0002
flight_rule.rationale:
Solar panel electrical harness has limited current carrying capability. Below 4.9 AU sun distance there's a risk the panel current will exceed the capability. MMPAT runs indicate that at 4.9 AU the max current the solar array can exceed the maximum rating for the solar panel electrical harness, allowing for worst case analysis (WCA) error in the current measurement. That is, 4.9 AU is the distance where measured current + WCA error = 12A, 12A being the maximum current limit setpoint.
As updating this parameter happens rarely, this is expected to be controlled by ground command.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Damage solar panel harness, reducing the amount of power the array can deliver to the spacecraft

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Total PSS and PME Main Bus Continuous Current Limit
flight_rule.description:
For periods over 2 minutes, the combined current on the 8 PSSs, PME-A Main, and PME-B Main busses shall be <= 45A.
See associated flight rules: PWR-A-0010, PWR-A-0011, PWR-A-0012, PWR-A-0003, PWR-A-0014
flight_rule.rationale: Thermal analysis shows that the PCDA operating temperatures will not exceed AFTs when processing <= 45A. DNG Req. 617176, L5-PCDA Power Output Current Capability. 45A constant current is driven by Peak Power ECR # 12655.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Exceed PCDA operational AFT.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Total PSS and PME Main Bus Current Limit for Less Than 2 Minutes
flight_rule.description:
If combined current on the 8 PSSs, PME-A Main, and PME-B Main busses is >45A and <= 66A, this can be for no more than 2 minutes, and no more often than 2 times in any rolling one hour period.
See associated flight rules: PWR-A-0003, PWR-A-0010, PWR-A-0011, PWR-A-0012, PWR-A-0013
flight_rule.rationale:
Thermal analysis shows that the PCDA operating temperatures will exceed AFTs when processing > 45A for more than 2 minutes.
Note that the scale of the excursion determines how long it takes for the AFT to be violated: an excursion of 66A will take less time to reach max AFT than an excursion of 46A.
The most reliable check on violating AFTs rely on PTM estimates of PCDA operating temperature. DNG Req. 617176, L5-PCDA Power Output Current Capability. 66A driven by the L4 ECR #18046.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Violate PCDA AFT. Possible hardware damage.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Ten Percent Maximum Transmit Duty Cycle
flight_rule.description:
The time during which REASON is transmitting per frequency (the 'transmit duty cycle') may not exceed ten percent (a) on a per cycle basis intra-dwell and (b) for any 2500 microsecond interval at dwell-to-dwell transitions. This rule should be evaluated for a 2500 microsecond running average at dwell-to-dwell transitions.
See associated flight rules: REAS-A-0008, REAS-A-0006, REAS-B-0002, REAS-A-0003
flight_rule.rationale:
The RF hardware, in particular the power amplifier unit (PAU), could be stressed if the duty cycle is exceeded. Short period violations (a few seconds) are unlikely to stress hardware. However, longer period violations (minutes) are likely to stress hardware.
Evaluating this rule over an Observation Plan cycle (defined in the CTD) does not by itself ensure that this requirement will be met. The per cycle evaluation is sufficient if the radar parameters do not change (as is frequently done in L5 RF testing) or for single dwell Observation Plans since these are equivalent to the intra-dwell scenario.
flight_rule.violation_impact: The RF hardware, in particular the power amplifier unit (PAU), could be stressed if the duty cycle is exceeded. Short period violations (a few seconds) are unlikely to stress hardware. However, longer period violations (minutes) are likely to stress hardware.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Maximum Duration for "Transmit Ready" State
flight_rule.description:
The maximum continuous duration allowed in the "Transmit Ready" state for the DSES is 310 microseconds.
See associated flight rules: REAS-A-0008, REAS-A-0005, REAS-B-0002, REAS-A-0003
flight_rule.rationale:
The RF hardware, in particular the power supply unit (PSU), could be stressed if this duration is exceeded.
Ideally, the "Transmit Ready" state should last no more than 60 microseconds longer than the transmit event itself, but can never exceed 310 microseconds total.
"Transmit ready" is the state of the RF subsystem when the PSU_DRIVER_ENABLE logical state is set to the Transmit position, rather than the Receive position, and includes the switching time of 30 micro sec. For more information, please see the "Obligations of Observation Plan" section of the "Europa REASON Event and Switch Timing Definition" D-101657.
flight_rule.violation_impact: The RF hardware, in particular the power amplifier unit (PAU), could be stressed if this duration is exceeded, and potentially result in permanent damage to the radar transmitters.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description:
Pre-delivery, checked vs. unchecked observation plans are segregated using GitHub/Cilix.
Post-Launch, REASON IOS will run this check on all Observation Plans prior to transfer to MOS for upload to S/C.
REASON has a Class B Observation Plan checker that should check the OP to ensure that the 310 microsecond duration is met. The OP checker needs to be run before any OP is uploaded. REASON I&T, SI&T, and REASON ISOC (or Mission Ops) will all need to run this checker. The Class C Observation Plan validator may flag transmit events lasting more than 60 microseconds longer than the transmit event with a warning.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Deploy REASON Antennas Near Earth
flight_rule.description:
Deploy the REASON antennas while the spacecraft is within the region between 0.97 AU and 1.1 AU from the Sun.
See associated flight rules: REAS-A-0007, REAS-A-0009, REAS-A-0010, REAS-B-0008
flight_rule.rationale:
This situation is motivated by requirement L4-REA-077: "The REASON instrument antenna shall be able to remain in the stowed antenna configuration, after launch and solar array deployment, while the spacecraft remains within the range of 0.97 AU and 1.1 AU from the Sun." This requirement was flowed to the antenna assemblies. The antennas have been designed to be stowed from 0.97 to 1.1 AU only. That means it might be unsafe if they remain stowed outside of 0.97 to 1.1 AU.
This constraint is driven by thermal and storage considerations.
flight_rule.violation_impact: The effect of long term storage and the thermal implications of delaying the deployments have not been evaluated, but could result in a failure to deploy the antennas successfully.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Seqgen will issue an error for this flight rule if the REASON antennas are not deployed when the spacecraft reach s/c to sun distance 1.1AU (~2024-341T12:13:47) after launch.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: No Concurrent Power ON for Both DSE units
flight_rule.description: Do not power on both Digital and Synthesizer Electronics (DSE) units, DSE-A and DSE-B, simultaneously.
flight_rule.rationale:
1) Only one DSE is needed for REASON operation. 2) Thermal analysis assumes that only one DSE is powered on at a time. 3) Powering both DSEs can potentially send conflicting control signals to the RF electronics, causing improper operation and loss of science data while both units are operating.
It is not possible to have both DSEs powered on at the same time via non PWR_PSS commanding.
flight_rule.violation_impact: 1) Powering both DSEs simultaneously may cause the DSES to approach thermal limits, however no damage will occur unless limits are violated. Fault protection should prevent this by powering down both DSEs. If this occurs during data collection, then science data may be lost. 2) Conflicting control signals sent by the DSES to the RF electronics may cause improper instrument operation leading to lost or degraded science data.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Solar Arrays in Standard Closest Approach (SCA) Configuration for REASON Activities
flight_rule.description:
When REASON is performing science activities or calibrations, (via the REAS_DO_SCIENCE command), the Solar Arrays need to be locked into the Standard Closest Approach (SCA) configuration of -90 degrees.
See associated flight rule: GNC-A-0015

The antenna elements are mounted on the SA, so the orientation of the SA determines the coupling between the S/C body and the antenna. If the SA is not in the correct orientation during a flyby, the antenna pattern will change, and the REASON SNR could be degraded.
flight_rule.violation_impact: The antenna pattern is dependent on the orientation of the antenna elements relative to the S/C body. The antenna elements are mounted on the SA, so the orientation of the SA determines the coupling between the S/C body and the antenna. If the SA is not in the correct orientation during a flyby, the antenna pattern will change, and the REASON SNR could be degraded.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Minimum Time Between Power Off and Power On of an RF Stack

Allowing less than 20 seconds between power on and power off will cause the overcurrent protection (OCP) in the power switch slice (PSS) to be activated resulting in power being cut off to the RF stack.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: REASON Cannot Transmit Within Two Million km of the Earth's Surface
flight_rule.description: The law is that you can't transmit RF within 2 million km of earth without a license from the National Telecommunications & Information Administration (NTIA), and REASON is not going to have one. As a consequence, we are legally not allowed to transmit when we are near earth. This rule does not restrict REASON being powered on, nor does it restrict REASON receiving RF. This is not related to the pointing of the spacecraft or the REASON antennas, only the location of the spacecraft relative to earth. This rule applies to both HF and VHF.
flight_rule.rationale: Legal compliance
flight_rule.violation_impact: In practice it is improbable that a violation would be detected. That said, although unlikely, someone might go to jail or be fined. More likely, would be embarrassment for JPL and NASA.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Observation Plan Upload Contingent on Plan Check Success
flight_rule.description:

See associated flight rules: REAS-A-0008, REAS-A-0006, REAS-C-0006, REAS-A-0005

The firmware on-board REASON does not check for hardware safety violations. The REASON Class B software checker checks for hardware safety issues in the OP prior to upload.
Note: The Class B software does not check to see if the plan makes sense or produces nominal science for a flyby. Class C software is used to generate the OP and to evaluate the science return from the OP.
flight_rule.violation_impact: There may be damage to the REASON hardware if the an OP is uploaded which has any destructive features that should be uncovered by the Class B Observation Plan Checker.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Observation Plan Upload Contingent on Testbed Checkout

All Observation Plans for post-launch activities shall be checked at the Spacecraft testbed before they can be uploaded to the flight system.
See associated flight rules: REAS-A-0008, REAS-A-0006, REAS-A-0005, REAS-C-0005
flight_rule.rationale: The Observation Plans used to command the radar through the flyby are complex, and the firmware on-board has no capability to check them. A small error in the Observation Plan could result in the loss of all REASON flyby science. Consequently, all Observation Plans need to be run through the testbed and operationally verified prior to use in flight. Post-delivery, REASON retains no hardware. All the engineering units, test units, and electronic ground support equipment are delivered to the Project. REASON's budget does not include software with the complexity and appropriate Class to find all possible errors.
flight_rule.violation_impact: A small error in the Observation Plan could result in the loss of all science data for a flyby.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Reassess Low Energy Trip threshold prior to eclipses
flight_rule.description: The low energy trip threshold parameter (SFP_MON_PWR_LOW_ENERGY_THRSH) shall be re-assessed prior to eclipses longer than 3 hours.
flight_rule.rationale: In order to prevent this the threshold must be reanalyzed and possibly updated prior to each eclipse such that there is enough energy between the low energy response and the UV to complete the eclipse.
flight_rule.violation_impact: If the low energy trip threshold is not changed, the spacecraft may trip low energy threshold during an eclipse and subsequently the hardware UV threshold and not be able to achieve a power positive state(as it is in eclipse). In this case the spacecraft could reach the deadbus condition.
