flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Both REUs are nominally turned "On"
flight_rule.description: All healthy REUs are nominally turned ON.
flight_rule.rationale:
Both REUs should be turned on to facilitate fault protection on the Prime REU and coordinated actions in the case of a PPROM activity.
If an REU must be inhibited, then to prevent conflicting PPROM actions we must inhibit the PPROM actions by send the hardware command to inhibit the REU.
If an REU must be inhibited, the hardware command to inhibit the REU must be sent by the ground. REU should be turned off with REU_POWER_STATE, before sending the hardware command to inhibit the REU.
If there is a need to uninhibit the REU, while the REU is off, send the hardware command to uninhibit the REU, then turn on the REU with REU_POWER_STATE. The ground can choose to send an extra REU_POWER_STATE to turn off the REU just in case and then uninhibit the REU.
flight_rule.violation_impact:
Single REU failure could lead to loss of mission.
Potentially conflicting PPROM commands and some ambiguity as to the time to recovery.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Instrument Recovery Attempt Clearing
flight_rule.description: The recovery_attempt_count variable needs to be cleared by the ground following recovery response execution prior to the next observation to allow for future recovery attempts.
flight_rule.rationale:
The recovery attempt count increments for each recovery response attempt that runs. It needs to be cleared by the ground to later allow for recovery again.
If the recovery count variable is not cleared, then future recovery attempts will be precluded as this variable is compared against the recovery attempt limit parameter in FSW. If the count variable is equal to or greater than the parameter, then recovery will not occur if the recovery monitor trips. Instead, the instrument will be powered off and marked sick.
flight_rule.violation_impact: If the variables are not cleared by the ground, recovery will not occur and the instrument will simply be turned off if the monitor trips. This violation is not a safety issue as it is safe to turn off the instruments, but we will not have recovery to gain science under recoverable faults.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Include as procedural steps in the instrument recovery procedure. Check the recovery count channel for the instrument in question, the state of the instrument (off/on, sick/healthy), and clear the recovery count variable to 0 via command to allow for future recovery attempts.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: FP Monitor/Response Parameters
flight_rule.description: Do not modify any FP monitor/response parameters (e.g. persistence/threshold values) without the approval of the FP team and monitor/response owners.
flight_rule.rationale: Modifying FP monitor/response parameters will affect the performance (e.g. timing and interference) of the FP design
flight_rule.violation_impact: Can be mission ending (e.g. flight system no longer detects and mitigates faults before time-to-critical-effect)

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Feed into ops procedures.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Clear Local Monitor Error Count Parameter
flight_rule.description: After a local monitor has tripped and after the anomaly investigation is complete, the error count parameter shall be reset to 0.
flight_rule.rationale: In order to effectively reset the monitor, the error count must be reset to 0. The local response does not operationally clear this counter.
flight_rule.violation_impact: The monitor is ineffective and unable to detect any subsequent faults. The exact impact depends on which monitor has tripped. All system level monitors will still be effective.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Feed into ops procedures.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Safing Behavior Parameters and CB TSRs
flight_rule.description: Every safing behavior parameter group (e.g., a "row" in the safing behavior parameter "table) should specify a Comm Behavior ID which points to the appropriate TSR file for the safemode data rate.
flight_rule.rationale: The objective of safe mode is to establish a deterministic and predictable end-state. Any CB configuration that safe mode invokes should have TSRs (which configure EVR/EHA rates) that are consistent with the downlink rate. Safe Mode and CB/EHA/TSR predictability
flight_rule.violation_impact: Inconsistent TSRs and downlink rates will result in dropped EVRs/EHAs and loss of visibility into the spacecraft.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Feed into ops procedure.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Instrument Science Recovery Parameter Updates
flight_rule.description: The RECOVERY_ATTEMPT_LIMIT parameter should be re-evaluated for each instrument to allow for recovery following characterization of each instrument during operations.
flight_rule.rationale:
The recovery attempt limit parameter needs to be updated from 0 to 1 to allow for recovery, otherwise the instrument will just be turned off.
0 is no recovery, 1 is 1 recovery attempt, 2 is 2 attempts and so on. It will be set to 0 for each instrument at the beginning of the mission, and only changed to 1 after the symptoms that trip the monitor are well understood. It should stay at 1 for the majority of the on-orbit mission after that, and only increased to 2 and above if deemed necessary and safe to allow for multiple recovery attempts.
flight_rule.violation_impact: If the parameters are not updated/cleared by the ground, recovery will not occur and the instrument will simply be turned off if the monitor trips. This violation is not a safety issue as it is safe to turn off the instruments, but we will not have recovery to gain science under recoverable faults.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Feed into ops procedure.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Safing Behavior Table
flight_rule.description: The Safing Behavior Table shall be reevaluated with any changes to: - the mission trajectory - telecom link analysis
flight_rule.rationale: Changes may have downstream effects on antenna choice in a safing scenario. In addition, the safety net uploss response is dependent on these entries.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Can be mission ending. May not be able to communicate with ground as a result of an incorrect entry.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Procedural steps in ops procedures that modify the items described above.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: High Voltage Commissioning Ramp Rate
flight_rule.description: During high voltage commissioning, once high voltage outputs exceed 1000 volts, do not exceed a commanded voltage increase of 100 volts/minute, averaged over one minute.
flight_rule.rationale:
When the sensor head, ion detector and high voltage power supply are exposed to atmosphere during ground testing, water vapor and other gasses may be absorbed in materials. The absorbed products will outgas over an extended period when exposed to high vacuum. The ability to outgas is dependent on pressure difference, venting rate, and temperature.
This flight rule needs to be implemented whenever the instrument is moved from atmosphere into vacuum, including for thermal vacuum testing, dust testing, and during on-orbit high voltage commissioning. Once completed, the high voltage can be ramped at the nominal value.
The FPGA controls the nominal/maximum ramp, which is 66.67 voltage/second or 1 volt/15 milliseconds.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Damage to the high voltage power supply, sensor head, ion detector, and/or high voltage cables from arcing.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description:
Compliance Verification:
Enforced by commanding voltage setpoint steps and dwell at each step long enough to satisfy the 100volt/min rule.
Operations team review of command products SUDA team to verify planned ramp rate for first high voltage ramp-up after launch does not exceed 100 volts/minute.
Commissioning sequence will use dwells (SUSPREL commands) after each setpoint step.
Will be included in SUDA procedure and SUDA sequences.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: No Decontamination before Door Deployment
flight_rule.description: A target decontamination activity shall not occur before the SUDA door has deployed.
flight_rule.rationale: Potential to exceed thermal protoflight temperature profile resulting in damaged hardware and internal particle redistribution (self-contamination) causing degraded science performance.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Damaged hardware and/or degraded science performance.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Ensure the THRM_ZONE_MODE, SUDA_TGT_DECON_ZN CLOSED_OP command is not sent before the SUDA_DOOR_DEPLOY

JPL team verify SUDA door has been deployed prior to decontamination activity
iSOC team verify SUDA door has been deployed prior to decontamination activity

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: No Decontamination Activities during Sun KoZ Violations
flight_rule.description: The sun must not be within the SUDA Sun Keep Out Zone of +/- 45 deg during any part of a decontamination activity, including the 2 hour cool-down after heaters are commanded off.
flight_rule.rationale:
Potential to exceed thermal proto-flight temperature profile resulting in damaged hardware
Decontamination Activities can take up to 12 hours including a 2 hour cool down period for the SUDA target to return to nominal temperatures after the heaters are turned off.
If contaminants remain on the target after a decontamination activity and a Sun Keep Out Zone (KoZ) violation occurs during the decontamination cool down period, the contaminants become photopolymerized causing a degradation in science performance.
A decontamination activity includes a 4-hour ramp-up at 1 deg C/minute to increase the temperature of the cold target (-95 deg C), an up to 6-hour decontamination at +120 deg C and 2 hour cool down period for a total of 12 hours.
The ramp period and subsequent four hour bake out at +120 deg C should remove the majority of the expected contaminates.
The 12-hour decontamination activity in full shall not be placed when the Sun is within SUDA Sun Sensitive KOZ. Sun impingement on a contaminated target may cause photopolymerization of those contaminants, potentially fixing them permanently to the target if the target is undergoing decontamination at the same time.
A contaminated target will be mitigated by performing decontamination activities to burn off contaminants. SUDA ISOC will be monitoring decontamination events to verify execution plans are as expected, verify activities were executed and were performed correctly.
The detector has a limited lifetime that is based on the amount of charge driven through it. When the detector is operating, signals from ionized dust particles and UV radiation are two sources that use up this lifetime. The detector is expected to have a 6 coulomb (C) life with little to no degradation expected before 4C. The expected amount of expended life by the end of mission, which includes an estimate of solar UV radiation exposure, estimates that 0.5C of life will be used. SUDA iSOC will be monitoring the accumulated charge through the detector.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Damaged hardware and a degradation in science performance.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: MERLIN to indicate warning if trying to plan decontamination activity while the Sun is within the SUDA Sun Sensitive KoZ
Ground System Software to identify when the Sun is within the SUDA Sun sensitive Keep Out Zone of +/- 45 degrees (SPICE kernels needed)

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Solar Constraint Violation Maximum Duration - Cruise
flight_rule.description:
During cruise, the SUDA target shall be decontaminated prior to a solar constraint violation if the duration of that violation is expected to exceed R^2 minutes (where R is defined as the distance from the Sun to the spacecraft in AU), the target is cold, and the target has not been decontaminated since the last contamination event. The R^2 number of minutes is the cumulative amount of sun KOZ violation time since the last decontamination.
See associated flight rules: SUDA-A-0007
flight_rule.rationale: UV from the sun can photopolymerize particles on the SUDA target. Sun exposure should be avoided until the target has been decontaminated.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Degraded science performance. May be permanent.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Decontamination Activity Cadence
flight_rule.description:
After the SUDA door has been deployed, the maximum span of time allowed between SUDA decontamination activities shall be no more than 4 weeks.
Related FRs: SUDA-A-0003
flight_rule.rationale: There is potential for S/C contamination and/or environmental contamination of the SUDA target. Periodically removing these reduces the chances of permanently stuck particles. Permanent contaminants will cause degraded science performance.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Permanent contamination of the target with photopolymerized material, leading to gradual degradation of instrument performance, impacting science deliverables.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: MERLIN will check Decontamination Activities and plan a Decontamination and/or alert the SUDA planner if there is a gap that violates this flight rule.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Decontamination Activities after a Contamination Event
flight_rule.description:
After the door is deployed and after a contamination event, there must be a decontamination activity before the next science collecting event.
A SUDA Contamination Event is defined in the Europa Clipper Mission Plan (D55485). Contamination Events do not affect SUDA when the door is closed, DECON heaters should not be turned on before door is deployed.
-------------------- From SUDA FDD (D-56164):
Decontamination should be conducted as soon as possible following contamination of the Target to prevent degradation. The SUDA Target is considered to be contaminated after: 1) Flybys of any planetary body at altitudes that bring the FS within the Hill sphere of that body. 2) Propulsive events imparting a delta-V larger than 8 m/s, as during these occurrences there is significant deposition of material (exospheric particles, thruster fuel) onto the SUDA Target. 3) At least 30 days have elapsed since the last SUDA Decontamination. SUDA Decontamination is scheduled by ground operators and will be executed via SC command sequences. SUDA expects SC Fault Management to abort a Decontamination activity in the event that the Sun drifts within a specified range of the SUDA KOZ. Decontamination activities should nominally only be conducted when the instrument is powered off.
flight_rule.rationale: Lack of contaminant removal from target will cause degraded science performance.
flight_rule.violation_impact:
Temporarily degraded SUDA target, and SUDA science data. Would require extra team work to analyze science data.
Contaminant particles will show up in science spectra. Ground processing can eventually average them out.
Contamination events do not affect the instrument before door open, so no decontamination is needed until door is open.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description:
MERLIN will identify Contamination Events and Science activities and confirm that there is a Decontamination Activity planned appropriately per this flight rule.
The decontamination event (including cool down) needs to end before the start of the science sequence. A rule of thumb is that the decontamination event should start at least 12 hours before the start of the science sequence.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Decontamination Heating Rate
flight_rule.description:
The Spacecraft-controlled decontamination heating rate of the SUDA target shall be no greater than 1degC/minute averaged over a four-hour duration.
The decontamination heaters are over-sized due to fault conditions for which we've had to design, so the tendency at BOL will be to exceed 1degC/minute. As the instrument ages and we learn more about the efficiency of the decontamination, we may change this to something else like a goal with a tolerance.
flight_rule.rationale:
If the target is heated at an average rate other than 1degC/minute, the target would not properly decontaminate resulting in degraded science.
The heating rate will be controlled via sequenced command timing of spacercraft-controlled heaters.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Degraded science

enforcement_method.enforcement_description:
Manual check by SUDA team
Compliance Verification: -SUDA team verify heating rate (using set points, dwell time, voltage of S/C, heaters in string, etc.).
-JPL team verify heating rate (TBD, may need to be SUDA only) (Heating rate variables may have set constraints or may be in feed forward data, TBD)

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: High Voltage Power Supply during Sun Keep Out Zone exposure
flight_rule.description: High Voltage Power Supply shall be powered off and SUDA in Idle mode (or powered off) when the Sun is within the SUDA Sun sensitive Keep Out Zone of +/-45 degrees.
flight_rule.rationale:
Charge driven through dynodes by UV photoelectrons degrades ion detector lifetime, which is a consumable.
Commands affected: SUDA SETHVOSC SUDA DISHVOSC
flight_rule.violation_impact: Reduced detector lifetime

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Anion (Negative) Mode Duration Under 5 minutes
flight_rule.description:
SUDA shall not remain in anion (negative) mode for periods exceeding 5 minutes when within 26.5 RJ of Jupiter.
Total lifetime amount of time spent in negative mode should not exceed 100 minutes.
flight_rule.rationale: Dense, energetic plasma on the target creates a strong secondary electron current flowing into the ion detector, decreasing its lifetime.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Decreased detector lifetime.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description:
SUDA SETHVPOL SUDA GOFLYBY SUDA GOSURVEY -Determines duration of flyby data acquisition based off of parameter input 20
Compliance verification: SUDA iSOC Constraint Checking software to report alarm if the instrument is in anion mode for a duration that is greater than [5 minutes] TBR SUDA team will track lifetime minutes in Anion mode for detector lifetime consumable.
TBD: Anion mode Activity with 5 minute duration and/or planning constraint?

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: SUDA Warm Target Mode - Cruise
flight_rule.description: When SUDA is powered off, operate the Decontamination heater in a low power mode from the moment the Target is exposed (SUDA Door deployment) until the first SUDA Decontamination activity post JOI.
flight_rule.rationale:
Keeping the Target temperature slightly warmer (~10 deg C) than that of the surrounding areas will significantly reduce the amount of material that settles onto the SUDA Target, mitigating the negative impacts of Sun exposure to SUDA since there is less material to photopolymerize.
After deployment of the SUDA Door, the SUDA Sensor Head is susceptible to contamination from interplanetary dust/particles, S/C outgassing, and thruster firings. Permanent degradation of the Target can occur when contaminants that have settled onto the SUDA Target are exposed to UV light, causing them to "stick" permanently onto the Target due to photopolymerization.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Increased risk of photopolymerization of particles on the sensor.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Sloan Swieso to determine.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Restricted SUDA S/C Commands
flight_rule.description: These commands should not be used in S/C sequences or in Real Time commands to the spacecraft without SUDA team waiver: SUDA_RESET_DATA_IF SUDA_RESET_COUNTER SUDA_DUAL_CMD SUDA_RAW_MEM_WRITE SUDA_POWER_ON_TO_BOOT SFP_SUDA_RECOVERY_COUNT_CLR SUDA_CLEAR_FAULT SUDA_RESET_INSTRUMENT SUDA_SET_AID_BIN SUDA_RAW_MEM_READ SUDA_PROCESS SUDA_CHG_MODE SUDA_TRANSMIT
flight_rule.rationale:
These commands can put SUDA into an unexpected configuration and/or obscure SUDA behavior. They should only be used in a fault recovery scenario.
These commands need an extra approval via waiver to ensure they are used correctly.
flight_rule.violation_impact:
Degraded Capability / Performance.
SUDA in unexpected configuration, loss of science data, loss of H&S data.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: SeqGen to issue warnings/errors on any S/C sequence or realtime command using any of these commands.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Cleanup Before Changing SUDA Modes
flight_rule.description: Any change mode command (from the S/C or from SUDA) must be preceded by commands HALTMEM and, when leaving a science mode, HALTSCI along with a command specific amount of time. HALTSCI requires 20 seconds to complete all science and HALTMEM requires 30 seconds.
flight_rule.rationale:
Changing modes while a science or memory operation is in progress can interfere with the operation. Commands HALTSCI and HALTMEM stop the operation and prevent loss of data.
The HALTSCI command stops the instrument from creating and saving science data, processing data, and transmitting data. These tasks are not allowed in IDLE mode and changing to IDLE mode while a science data related task is still running will cause memory write errors that prevent SUDA from executing any other activities. We were only able to clear the errors on the SUDA EM by power cycling the instrument.
The HALTMEM command stops the instrument from performing any memory task that it is involved in including shuffle, memory dumps, and memory writes. Some memory tasks are only allowed in certain modes and changing to a disallowed mode would cause errors.
Delaying data and increasing commanding impacts the team's ability to configure for the next flyby.
flight_rule.violation_impact: No memory or science activities after this error will be executed. Potential loss of Science Data, loss of redundant memory sections, knowledge and/or delayed data. A shutdown command from the S/C is sequenced after every SUDA activity (for power modeling and insurance against a hung sequence or other issues) and will force SUDA through a power cycle clearing the problem. Additional commanding will be needed to resend science data and to regain memory knowledge.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: SUDA will check SUDA sequences for compliance. SUDA will review any use of SUDA_CHG_MODE command on the S/C for correct use.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: SUDA Decontamination Heaters and Instrument Should Not Be On at the Same Time
flight_rule.description: The SUDA instrument and the decontamination heaters should not be powered on at the same time to prevent SUDA from using more power than planned. If the spacecraft-controlled decontamination heaters are in either Decontamination or Warm Target Mode, do not power SUDA on. If the SUDA instrument is powered on, do not power the decontamination heaters.
flight_rule.rationale: SUDA's design and conops assumes that we will not use the decon heaters at the same time as the instrument to fit into our power allocations
flight_rule.violation_impact: Increased SUDA power and energy consumption that will impact the spacecraft power and energy resources.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: scheduling constraint as SUDA activities

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: SUDA shutdown and reset sequence constraints
flight_rule.description:
The onboard reset sequence (sequence run after a reset command is received from either the S/C or internal SUDA sequence) must complete in 30 seconds or less in order to complete its tasks before the reset occurs.
The onboard shutdown sequence (sequence run after a shutdown command is received from either the S/C or internal SUDA sequence) must complete in 55 seconds or less in order to complete its tasks before the shutdown occurs.
flight_rule.rationale: SUDA uses sequences to configure for a reset and a shutdown. The agreement with the S/C (requirements copied below) sets a time of 30 seconds for the reset behavior to complete and 60 seconds for the shutdown behavior.
flight_rule.violation_impact: SUDA not in safe state for shutdown/reset. Possible delay of Science data transmission and require extra ORC commanding to complete pre-shutdown activities. Or no impact depending on SUDA activities at the time.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: Check SUDA internal scripts and review.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: RCS System Mode below 1.3 AU
flight_rule.description: While the spacecraft is less than 1.3 AU from the Sun, SYS_RCS_NOMINAL / SYS_RCS_STANDBY / SYS_SAFE_STANDARD must be used instead of SYS_RWA_NOMINAL / SYS_RWA_STANDBY, even when the spacecraft is under RWA control.
flight_rule.rationale:
Waiver ECWB-1496: RWA safing timelines are too long for thermal survivability of instruments. Setting the system mode to SYS_RCS will ensure that safe modes use RCS, not RWA. The spacecraft can be controlled on RWA nominally despite the system mode being set to SYS_RCS.
Included SYS_SAFE_STANDARD as that is the nominal end state after launch.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Permanent damage to instrument due to thermal PFT exceedances.

reference_info.reference_document: Waiver ECWB-1496

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: SEQGen will create an attribute in the SM model. This attribute will be set by command "SM_CHANGE_MODE". If this command is executed while the S/C to sun distance is < 1.3AU and the parameter value is not one of these values, SEQGen will flag an error: "SYS_RCS_NOMINAL", "SYS_RCS_STANDBY", "SYS_SAFE_STANDARD"

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Threshold for Updating VCS Mass Properties
flight_rule.description: Except for JOI, parameters for VCS mass properties shall be updated to maintain on-board system moments of inertia for all axes within +/-2.5% of the current ground estimate. After the JOI Demo and prior to JOI, VCS mass properties shall be updated to the predicted arithmetic average inertia over JOI. After JOI and prior to RWA-flybys, VCS mass properties shall be updated to comply with the limit of +/-2.5%.
flight_rule.rationale:
Ixx varies ~40% over the mission and is driving. Iyy varies only ~7% over the mission, and Izz ~1%. All controllers are designed to incorporate the maximum driving variation between updates, which is +/-8% in Ixx over JOI since could be operating at either end of JOI. Interplanetary DV99 shifts Ixx only ~-0.4%. So FR is primarily for achieving "reasonable" precision in RWC feedforward/gyroscopic-compensation for slews and flybys without requiring frequent parameter updates. A 5% (=+/-2.5%) Ixx update threshold requires VCS parameter updates only once or twice a year.
Since GNC L4 V&V needs to vary the "error" in the VCS mass properties, this 2.5% becomes an assumption of L4 V&V. It does NOT mean that if hit, say, 2.6% then science pointing is violated. There is pointing margin. But it would require re-analysis.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Possible attitude control instability for JOI setting. For Tour, reduced science pointing performance. (The "2.5%" of this FR is baked into GNC L4 V&V.)

enforcement_method.enforcement_description: A manual Systems check.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: RF Coax Transfer switch should not be actuated
flight_rule.description: The Coax Transfer Switch (CTS) shall not be commanded to change position.
flight_rule.rationale:
To prevent this switch from leading to a stuck in-between mission ending failure mode, this switch should not be nominally actuated in flight, including during flight system characterization.
The CTS controls which radio is connected to which diplexer. Nominally, Radio A is connected to diplexer A and Radio B is connected to diplexer B. If multiple failures occur in the telecom subsystem, it may be necessary to use Radio A with diplexer B or Radio B with diplexer A and this would necessitate actuating the CTS. See Memorandum Europa-4900-2017-020.
Note that the SFP_DESIRED_CTS_CONFIGURATION parameter also exists and is used by FP in the uploss response and by TEL in TEL_SEL_PATH as an additional safeguard. These behaviors check the value of the SFP_DESIRED_CTS_CONFIGURATION parameter and will not actuate the CTS if the desired position does not match this parameter.
The SFP_DESIRED_CTS_CONFIGURATION parameter should be nominally set to the same value on both ECEs.
flight_rule.violation_impact: A stick in-between failure of the Coax Transfer switch will result in permanent loss of uplink and by consequence, a loss of mission.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Do not actuate RF switches while X-band exciter is enabled.
flight_rule.description: RF switches should not be actuated while either X-band exciter A or B is enabled.
flight_rule.rationale: Switch degradation over time would occur if hot switching is performed. X-band exciter should be disabled prior to actuating RF switches. Note: Antenna Selection Behavior handles this and power off the X-band exciters prior to actuating RF switches.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Possible damage to telecom hardware

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: At least one radio powered on at all times
flight_rule.description:
At least one of the radios should be powered on at all times.
See associated flight rule: TEL-B-0001
flight_rule.rationale: Need to always have the spacecraft capable of receiving commands. Need to have spacecraft available for uplink commands from the ground, which could be needed at any time. Radios are powered on into the receive-only state.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Loss of comm and therefore loss of control of the spacecraft, possible loss of mission.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: RF WTS-4 Restriction in Inner Cruise
flight_rule.description: WTS-4 should not be actuated in flight (including flight system characterization) until after the completion of the Inner Cruise mission sub-phase.
flight_rule.rationale: A stuck in-between failure of WTS4 will result in the loss of the +Y LGA, the -Y-Z FBA, and the +Y-Z FBA. The +Y-Z FBA has the important role to be used for Inner Cruise communications when the SPE angle is greater than 90 degrees. During Inner Cruise, the flight system -Y axis is pointed at the Sun for thermal reasons, and for the indirect trajectory cases, there are several periods of time when Earth will be in the +Y hemisphere. The stuck in-between failure of WTS4 would result in losing communications during these periods.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Possible loss of the +Y LGA, the -Y-Z FBA and the +Y-Z FBA. Loss of comm in inner cruise.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description:
DT 8/23/21 - SEQGen will monitor the command "TEL_CFG_RF_SWITCH" and attribute "WTS_4_position" to make sure it's position does not change during the inner cruise time period.
If it is determined that this FR should be implemented in Merlin, here is a potential FOL that can be used to implement it. This FOL description references states, and enforcement will be at the activity planning level in Merlin

FOL Evaluation Description: List of Windows that contain all the times when RF WTS-4 is being actuated before inner cruise phase. Any Windows that are returned are in VIOLATION.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Do not use Ka-band dual polarization mode
flight_rule.description:
Do not use Ka-band dual polarization mode.
Ka-band dual polarization mode may be entered by the following commanding: (CB_CFG_TELECOM or CB_CFG_TELECOM_GROUP with a Ka-band radio mode), followed by a TEL_POWER_TWTA command specifying the backup Ka-band TWTA.
flight_rule.rationale: Thermal analysis of the dual polarization Ka-band mode at 4.9 AU solar range shows that the radio AFT will be exceeded by 1.5 degrees. The 5.6 AU solar range case has the radio interface at 28.8 C, which is a 16.2 C of AFT margin. If the radio part most susceptible to reliability degradation (NBB-400) is operated continuously at 1.5 degrees above the AFT, the MTTF will decrease from 1,968 years to 1,747 years. In order to use dual polarization Ka-band mode, thermal analysis must show that the radio will not exceed its AFT, or a waiver for the exceedences described in ECWB-835 and ECWB-3307 is processed.
flight_rule.violation_impact: The radio AFT will be exceeded by 1.5 degrees. If the radio part most susceptible to reliability degradation (NBB-400) is operated continuously at 1.5 degrees above the AFT, the MTTF will decrease from 1,968 years to 1,747 years.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Periodic Radio Power Cycling
flight_rule.description:
Each powered radio should be power cycled at least every 6 months.
See associated flight rules: TEL-A-0005
flight_rule.rationale: Minimizes potential for undetected radiation effect states as supplementary mitigation for critical events. Need to have radio working during critical events, so recommendation from radio team is to power cycle radio every 3-6 months for supplementary mitigation for undetected radiation effects. Wait 60 seconds to clear any radiation induced effects before powering back on. ConOps used typically by APL missions.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: If in a downlink mode, do not use Radio Mission Mode to go to another downlink mode.
flight_rule.description: If in a downlink mode (with radio exciter enabled), do not use Radio Mission Mode to go to another downlink mode with the same band (and the same radio exciter enabled).
flight_rule.rationale:
If in a downlink mode (with radio exciter enabled), do not use Radio Mission Mode to go to another downlink mode with the same band (and the same radio exciter enabled). First switch to the receive-only mode, then use the Radio Mission Mode command to switch to the desired downlink mode. If the radio is sent into a downlink mode while it is already in a mode with the same band powered, there is a chance that a synthesizer will not be configured correctly and prevent the radio from being able to downlink on the correct frequency. When the radio is in this state, it can be recovered by putting the radio in Receive only mode. Documented in the Radio User's Guide, Section 5.2.
If in mode 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 11, 12, 41 (any X-band mode), do not use the Radio mission mode command with mode 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 11, 12, 41 (any X-band mode).
If in mode 7, 8, 21, or 22 (any Ka-band mode), do not use Radio mission mode command with mode 7, 8, 21, or 22 (any Ka-band mode).
Note that using comm behavior will prevent violation of this rule.
flight_rule.violation_impact: No downlink or downlink at an incorrect frequency

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Minimum wait for radio power cycle or firmware reset
flight_rule.description: Allow at least 10 seconds after a radio power cycle or firmware reset command prior to enabling a mode with the exciter enabled (and radio transmitting). Allow at least 2 seconds after a radio power cycle or firmware reset command prior to issuing any other command to the radio. Note: the radio power on behavior already includes a 10 second wait.
flight_rule.rationale: The radio needs ~10 seconds for the internal oscillator and radio thermal time constants to settles. This is a conservative number. The radio needs ~2 seconds to boot before it can accept commands. Sending commands before the radio is finished booting will result in a fault.
flight_rule.violation_impact: The internal oscillator and radio thermal time constants will not have settled so the transmitted frequency will not be as stable. Sending a command to the radio before it is finished booting may result in a fault.

The non-prime radio downlink underflow counter will increase. The non-prime radio will output a 1/0 pattern if nothing was received after the encoder core was reset. If there was data received after that reset the last frame will be repeated.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Ka-band dual polarization mode should not be used at Sun ranges < 4.9 AU

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Repeating Hardware Commands
flight_rule.description:
Don't send the same hardware command (VC-0) multiple times consecutively, within a single VC-5 session.
Impacted commands are any with "type" = "hw_command"
flight_rule.rationale:
If hardware commands (VC-0) are sent multiple times, they will each be executed. Depending on the command, this can have mission ending consequences.
Note that this is different than immediate commands (VC-1). In a single uplink session (bookended by VC-5 frames), only the first valid VC-1 will be accepted, the duplicates will be ignored.
Hardware commands bypass FSW safety nets. Repeating these commands is likely unnecessary.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Hardware commands are inherently dangerous on spacecraft, if they are repeated with poor timing it can have mission ending consequences.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: UVS Solar Polymerization Protection
flight_rule.description:
The UVS Airglow Port boresight shall not be pointed within 10 degrees cross-track and along-track (10-degree half angle square) of the unocculted Sun while the Airglow Port door is open.
See associated flight rule: UVS-B-0002
flight_rule.rationale: To prevent polymerization of contaminants on optical elements. Level of concern is a total cumulative exposure (over the life of the mission) of more than 120 hours at 1 Astronomical Unit equivalent illumination (1/R^2). Might be cases where the sun angle violates this limitation but the sun is eclipsed by Europa. UVS plans to observe Europa's nightside (occulted sun). Any waiver or accidental violation should track and consider this 120 hour condition.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Violation has the potential to permanently affix contaminants onto the optics, permanently reducing UVS sensitivity so that it will not achieve science objectives.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: UVS Instrument During Engine Activities
flight_rule.description: The UVS shall have the high voltage powered off and the Airglow Port door closed during planned engine activities.
flight_rule.rationale: To prevent contamination to the instrument internal hardware and/or damage to the high voltage. Engine activities = any thruster firing.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Violation has the potential to degrade science operations (contamination) and/or permanent damage the instrument electronics and loss of UVS.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: UVS Airglow Port Door Closure Before Instrument Power Down
flight_rule.description: Neither the UVS_POWER_OFF_IMM command nor the PWR_PSS_POWER_STATIC_SW command with arguments [<any>, PWR_PCDA_PSS_6_2A_SW_12, <any>, OPEN] shall be issued.
flight_rule.rationale:
To prevent contaminants on the optical elements.
The nominal power down behavior sends the instrument to SAFE mode prior to powering down, which should close the aperture door (corresponding parameters must be set appropriately). The UVS_POWER_OFF command kicks off that behavior and should be the only command used to power off the instrument in nominal sequence planning.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Violation has the potential to allow contamination to accumulate on the primary mirror, permanently reducing UVS sensitivity so that it will not achieve science objectives.

enforcement_method.enforcement_description:
DT 09/27/2021 SEQGen will flag this FR if the command UVS_POWER_OFF_IMM is issued.
Or if command PWR_PSS_POWER_STATIC_SW is executed with the second and forth arguments equal to "PWR_PCDA_PSS_6_2A_SW_12" and OPEN.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: UVS Instrument Following Engine Activities (High Voltage)
flight_rule.description:
The UVS shall not be commanded to activate the high voltage for 30min after planned engine activities.
See related flight rule: UVS-A-0012
flight_rule.rationale: To prevent damage to the instrument internal hardware and/or damage to the high voltage. Engine activities = any thruster firing.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Violation has the potential to damage the instrument electronics.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: UVS Instrument Following Engine Activities (Airglow Port Door)
flight_rule.description:
The UVS shall not be commanded to open the Airglow Port door for 30min after planned engine activities.
See related flight rule: UVS-A-0011
flight_rule.rationale: To prevent contamination of the instrument internal hardware and/or damage to the high voltage. Engine activities = any thruster firing.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Violation has the potential to allow contamination to accumulate on the primary mirror, permanently reducing UVS sensitivity so that it will not achieve science objectives.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: UVS Excessive Solar Count Rates
flight_rule.description:
The UVS Airglow Port boresight shall not be pointed within 20 degrees cross-track and along-track (20 degree half angle square) of the unocculted Sun when the Airglow Port Door is open and when the detector high voltage is on.
See associated flight rule: UVS-A-0006
flight_rule.rationale:
To prevent excessive detector count rates.
Might be cases where the sun angle violates this limitation but the sun is eclipsed by Europa.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Violation will cause the instrument to safe (via internal instrument fault protection), which will shut down high voltage, and close the Airglow Port door. Any active observations will be stopped, resulting in a partial loss of science.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: UVS Warm-Up Thermal Protection
flight_rule.description: The command to power on UVS (UVS_POWER_ON) must not be issued less than 5 hours after transitioning the UVS Zone temperature control setpoints from non-operating limits to operating limits (THRM_ZONE_MODE, UVS_ZN, CLOSED_OP).
flight_rule.rationale:
To ensure that the instrument is at the proper temperature to power on.
The survival heater non-operational set "On" point is -18 C (2 C degrees offset) from minimum non-operational. The survival heater set "Off" point is -15 C degree. This provides a 3 C degree deadband for the UVS survival heater to operate.
The minimum operational temperature limit for UVS is -5 C degrees. The time duration in this flight rule is the estimated length of time that it will take the instrument to warm up from the non-operational temperature to -5 C degrees assuming cold thermal conditions.
Based on the correlated thermal model and report submitted by UVS, the expected maximum duration (cold case, lowest voltage) to heat UVS from non-op to operating temperatures is ~5 hours. This covers the time from the start of warm-up at the nonoperational temperature to heat soak (1 cycle of heater control band) based on the worst case cold condition.
flight_rule.violation_impact: The flight system behavior for powering on UVS does have a temperature check (checks for temperature > -5 C), but if UVS is not at that minimum operational temperature the power-on behavior will error (i.e. not keep trying).

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: Streaming UVS Data to the BDS during a filter operation
flight_rule.description: UVS shall be powered off during BDS filter, copy, and radiation maintenance operations.
flight_rule.rationale: While the BDS is performing these operations, it is not recording new data.
flight_rule.violation_impact: If UVS sends any data to the BDS while the BDS is performing these operations, the data will be lost.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: UVS Critical Commanding
flight_rule.description: Any time a UVS critical command is sent, a corresponding critical confirm command that specifies the critical command must be sent within 30 seconds to execute properly.
flight_rule.rationale:
A subset of UVS instrument commands are considered UVS critical commands. (Note these are different from system constrained commands in FSW).
If a UVS critical command is sent but a critical confirm is not sent within 30 seconds, the command will not be executed.
flight_rule.violation_impact: Depending on the command and subsequent commanding interactions, parameters (including high voltage settings) or door positioning or science collection could be impacted.

flight_rule.flight_rule_title: UVS ASRT-150 AIDs mapping to Bin ID
flight_rule.description: Per IICD ASRT-150, Instrument science data packets associated with a Accountability Identifier (AID) should all be assigned the same bin-id in BDS (i.e., all of the data associated with an AID is in a single bin). This approach allows more rapid downlink and assessment of the completeness of an accountable data product since all of the instrument science data packets associated with the AID are in a single BDS bin
flight_rule.rationale: The instrument FSW/FW does not enforce a mapping between packets with the same AID to have the same bin ID. Instead, any mapping is enforced by the SIOS team during the command process. So for the instrument to comply with ASRT-150, they need to enforce this FR in ops instead.
flight_rule.violation_impact:
Multiple BDS bins will need to be downloaded in order to assess the completeness of the AID. Since BDS bins are related to downlink priority, you may need to wait for ALL data in multiple bins to be downloaded before you can assess the completeness of the Accountable Data Product. Note that whether ASRT-150 is met or not, the science data would still be downloaded and available. However, not complying with ASRT-150 may result in the process of determining whether or not all of the data that was expected as part of an AID more difficult and time consuming.
Question for Thom: would the violation ever be considered to be "loss of data"? (If so this would be a Cat-B)
